findings.ruling_reason: Claim 90's steps (tube stock, laser cutting, fixture shape-setting, heating, water quench) carry no process feature beyond what is needed to make the product. The sealing edge and convoluted wall are product features, and [0147]-[0150] assert no process effect. Claim 90 therefore stands or falls with the ring, which F-32-1 shows is exposed. Caveat for counsel: no saved reference documents this NiTi tube-processing route; that it is standard is a general technical point an examiner would readily support with documents from the tube-component field. High stands. Lead finding; F-32-3 is a duplicate.

findings.title: Claim 90 is the standard superelastic NiTi tube-processing route
findings.attack: Laser cutting NiTi tube, shape-setting in a constraining fixture with heat and quench, and electropolishing are the standard route; the sealing edge and convoluted wall are the shape set, not process features.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Make claim 90 recite manufacture of the seat ring of amended claim 67 and add the press-in step of claim 100; narrowing.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-32-2: the same objection that claim 90 is the standard superelastic NiTi tube-processing route, with the product features, not process features, as its only difference. Its remedy (tie claim 90 to the amended claim 67 ring and to the press-in step of claim 100) is one of the options under F-32-2.

findings.title: Every independent claim ties the purge to over-travel of the poppet caused by the pressure differential
findings.attack: Depressor or hand over-travel [0066], a separate purge actuator with the poppet on its normal stroke only [0123], and Schrader cores opened by the head pin [0137] all fall outside claims 1, 58 and 79; claim 57 describes a combination a competitor would not build; if F-32-2 shows depression, the tested embodiment is outside the claims too.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Define the purge state by the poppet or a deflecting formation moving with it being beyond the normal stroke, with the pressure-differential trigger and mechanical depression as sibling dependent claims; or add an independent claim with a deflecting formation driven by the poppet or a pressure-responsive purge actuator.
findings.ruling_reason: Claims 1 and 58 define the purge state as occurring 'at a pressure differential exceeding the over-travel threshold, in which the poppet is in over-travel', and claim 79 requires 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold, whereby the poppet moves into over-travel'. The description discloses three routes outside that wording: over-travel by a depressor or by hand 'whatever the pressure differential', with the second spring stage omitted ([0066]); a separate purge actuator carrying the deflecting formation 'the poppet (40) performing only its normal stroke' ([0123]); and Schrader poppets depressed by the pump head ([0137]). A competitor with a single-rate spring and pin-driven over-travel, or with an actuator, escapes claims 1, 58 and 79. In the US, disclosed but unclaimed subject matter risks dedication to the public. Claim 46 adds depression only as an extra to the pressure-driven device, and claim 57 keeps the pressure trigger. High is right. The proposed remedy keeps the normal-stroke/over-travel structure. The purge-actuator limb of F-32-6 is carried here.

findings.title: Figure plan and registry contain drafting-process content and a self-contradictory FIG. 1 instruction
findings.attack: Prompt numbers, DA codes, sketch filenames, 'no image has been seen', 'the inventor states doubt', and an instruction to footnote an assumption on a drawing sheet; the FIG. 1 instruction cannot be drawn as written.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Strip every internal reference from the draftsperson instructions, delete the FIG. 6 footnote instruction and state one at-rest condition for FIG. 1.
findings.ruling_reason: The figure plan contains drafting-process content: 'Prompt 16 (blueprint) has not yet run'; DA codes, C-codes and prompt numbers ('01 Q22', '11.md', '14.md'); sketch filenames ('FIG-1.png'); 'no image has been seen'; 'the inventor states doubt about pursuing it'. The FIG. 6 entry cites 'the drawing convention adopted to reconcile' the interference fit with the outward deflection. FIG. 1 asks for the 'purge gap (shown closed)' as a numbered component, which cannot be drawn without showing a clearance at rest that contradicts the closed state; the substantive contradiction is F-30-6. Severity is corrected to medium. These are draftsperson instructions, not application text. No claim is affected, and the clean-up can be done in place before drawings are commissioned, but it must happen before any sheet is drawn. Lead finding for the figure-instruction content; F-30-16 and F-30-25 are duplicates in part.

findings.title: Purge-on-every-opening and separate purge actuator disclosed at [0051] and [0123] and excluded by every independent claim
findings.attack: A single-rate spring with the shoulder engaging the ring from the start of the stroke, or an annular piston purge actuator with the poppet on its normal stroke only, is outside claim 1's normal-open state and poppet-driven deflection; the competitor cites the applicant's own description.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an alternative independent claim without the normal-open-state requirement on [0051] and a claim to the purge actuator on [0123].
findings.ruling_reason: Upheld on the [0051] limb; the [0123] purge-actuator limb duplicates F-32-4. [0051] discloses setting the threshold 'close to the crack pressure, so that the purge state is reached on substantially every opening', with a single-rate spring. A variant in which the shoulder engages from the start of the stroke has no normal-open state and falls outside claims 1, 58 and 79, all of which require one. Claim 40 (single-rate spring, threshold set by ring stiffness) still requires the normal-open state of claim 1. Severity is corrected to medium: the escape is credible, but the proposed independent claim without a normal-open state gives up the normal-stroke/over-travel sequence. INDEX.md reports that sequence (N3+N4) as undisclosed in any saved reference; the saved art includes two-threshold second paths (#14, #16). Whether to claim it is a scope-against-validity choice for counsel, not a defect in the text.

findings.title: The test evidence does not show that the pressure differential drives over-travel
findings.attack: With a floor pump the differential across the poppet should fall between strokes and go negative on removal, yet the snap was heard only on removal. That is at least as consistent with the pump head holding the poppet in over-travel ([0066]) as with the claimed pressure-driven mechanism. How a 3.5 bar differential develops across an open main passage is not explained, and travel was not measured.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Obtain the pump head type, whether it bears on the poppet, whether a snap occurred between strokes, and any measurement of differential or travel; add that disclosure and correct [0044], [0068] and [0158].
findings.ruling_reason: On the text the finding is right: the evidence does not show which mechanism produced over-travel. [0165]: over-travel 'indicated only by the audible snap'. [0158]: the snap was heard 'on removal of the inflation device', and [0158] adds that it 'is not a measurement of the over-travel distance'. Travel and pressure differential were not measured ([0156]). With a floor pump, the differential across an open poppet should fall to about the crack pressure between strokes. A purely pressure-driven over-travel would then be expected to recover between strokes, not only on removal, as [0044] ('as occurs when the inflation device is removed') and [0068] assume. A pump head bearing on the poppet ([0066]) fits the reported observation at least as well. Whether P-1 to P-3 were pressure-driven turns on facts outside the package: the pump head type and whether it bears on the poppet tip; whether a snap was heard between strokes; any pressure trace across the core; and whether the lock nut was open. If the head depressed the poppet, the tested embodiment sits outside claims 1, 58 and 79 (see F-32-4), and [0044], [0068], [0158] and [0179] need correcting. High stands.

findings.title: Background, field, summary and brief description of drawings missing; [0160] dangling
findings.attack: Required sections and the abstract are absent; [0160] refers to failure modes described in a background that does not exist, in the paragraph reporting the comparison on which the effect rests.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the missing sections with an acknowledgment of the saved background art, and supply or reword the background that [0160] relies on.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-30-21: same missing field, background, summary, brief description of drawings and abstract, and the same dangling reference to 'the background' in [0160].

findings.title: Carried by the core body, read with [0005] and [0117]
findings.attack: Read with [0005], a poppet-mounted ring is indirectly carried by the core body, which widens the prior art that reads on claim 1; [0117]'s contrast lets a defendant using the inverted arrangement argue it is excluded. Scope is uncertain either way.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite a deflectable ring element carried by one of the core body and the poppet and a deflecting formation carried by the other, with the core-body-held arrangement dependent.
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 1 recites the ring 'carried by the core body'. [0005] says 'carried by' covers indirect carriage 'through one or more intervening components'. A skirt on the poppet, which the core body guides, is therefore arguably carried by the core body, and that widens the art that reads on claim 1 (e.g. rings or wipers on the moving member, #3 and #13). Conversely, [0117] contrasts the inverted skirt 'carried by the poppet' with the ring 'held in the core body', which gives a defendant with the inverted arrangement an exclusion argument. Claim 24 (integral flexure) and claim 18 (retained against an internal shoulder) do not settle it. The scope is uncertain in both directions. Medium stands.

findings.title: Claim 1: the technical effect is not credibly shown, which opens a combination attack
findings.attack: Claim 1's only claimed effect is the air purge, which the data do not isolate and which did not clean the purge region; the problem may be reformulated as an alternative second flow path, with index #16 or #14 (two-threshold second paths) combined with #1 (radially deflecting NiTi ring). Motivation is thin, hence medium.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add data isolating the air purge before filing or within the priority year, state the effect of the separate purge path explicitly, and keep claims 25 and 47 as fallbacks.
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 1 recites the purge flow path but not the wipe (claim 25). Its effect is therefore the air purge, which the text does not isolate ([0167]: 'no attribution between them is made herein') and which left film in the purge region ([0159]). An examiner can treat the problem as an alternative second flow path. Saved #16 (US 8,043,186 B2: a second, spring-set annular orifice opening at a higher pressure) and #14 (EP 1137892 A1: apertures uncovered above a set pressure in a tyre valve core) supply the two-threshold second path, and #1 supplies a radially displacing wave ring. The answer is that nothing in those references suggests opening the second path by over-travel of the same poppet deforming a ring that closes on recovery ([0048], [0112]). INDEX.md records no saved reference with N3+N4 combined. Motivation is thin, so medium stands. Distinct from F-30-11, which carries breadth and sufficiency.

findings.title: Claim 31 inconsistent with claim 1's 'separate from the main passage ... from the supply side'
findings.attack: In claim 31 the supply side reaches the inner-surface gap only through the lifted sealing face, so the purge flow path is not separate from the main passage from the supply side.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate claim 31 to state the purge gap communicates with the supply side through the open main passage and is distinct from it.
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 31 places the purge gap 'bounded by an inner surface of the seat ring and the poppet on the chamber side of the sealing edge'. Gas from the supply side can reach that gap only by first passing the lifted sealing face, which is the main passage ([0019], [0045]). That conflicts with claim 1's 'purge flow path (62), separate from the main passage, extends from the supply side through the purge gap'. [0105] asserts the gap 'remains a flow path distinct from the main passage' but does not explain how, given that main-passage flow also runs through the seat ring bore. The rewording offered (communicates through the open main passage, and is distinct from it) matches [0105]. Medium stands. The claim 31 limb of F-30-12 is carried here.

findings.title: Claim 46 omits the closing feature of claim 1
findings.attack: With a depressor holding the poppet in over-travel the gap does not close when the pressure differential falls, so claim 46 lacks a limitation of claim 1.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate the closing clause of claim 1 as occurring when the load applied by the poppet to the ring is removed.
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 46 says the poppet is 'additionally movable into over-travel by mechanical depression'. 'Additionally' leaves every state of claim 1 intact whenever the poppet is not depressed. Claim 1 is an apparatus claim whose states are responses to the pressure differential, and the depressor sits in the inflation device or an adaptor, not in the claimed valve core. When the depressor is withdrawn, the ring recovers and closes the gap as claim 1 requires. [0066] supports over-travel by depression 'in addition' to the pressure-driven route. There is no contradiction between claims 46 and 1. The proposed rewording of claim 1's closing clause (closing when the poppet's load on the ring is removed, [0060]/[0098]) is still useful for the design-around in F-32-4.

findings.title: Clarity terms in claims 1, 44, 49, 55, 64
findings.attack: 'associated with', a 'closed' gap, 'at-rest form' defined by an unclaimed purge shoulder, 'about' with no tolerance, 'nominally', 'low-adhesion', 'tyre set-up'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate each from existing description text without changing scope, as set out in objection 14.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-30-15 (the same reviewer's fuller list): 'associated with', 'closed' gap, 'at-rest form', 'about', 'nominally', 'low-adhesion' and 'tyre set-up' in claims 1, 44, 49, 55 and 64, with the same citations ([0007], [0010], [0025], [0045], [0129]). Ruled under F-30-15, F-30-19 and F-30-23.

findings.title: Closing the purge gap when the differential falls below the over-travel threshold, versus hysteresis
findings.attack: Superelastic unloading hysteresis, and spring friction, can keep the gap open until the differential is well below the threshold at which it deflected; a defendant argues the closing condition of claims 1 and 58 is not met literally.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Replace with closing the purge gap as the pressure differential falls, as claim 79 already words it; no loss of scope.
findings.ruling_reason: Claims 1 and 58 require the ring to close the purge gap 'when the pressure differential falls below the over-travel threshold'. [0074] acknowledges that NiTi has a transformation hysteresis (NiTiCu is offered for a 'narrower transformation hysteresis'), so superelastic unloading occurs below the loading level. Friction in the spring adds to the lag. A defendant can argue the gap stays open below the threshold and closes only at a lower value, so the literal condition is not met. This can be said even of the preferred NiTi embodiment. Claim 79 already avoids the problem ('whereby the pressure differential falls and the deflectable ring element ... closes the purge gap'), and adopting that wording costs no scope. Medium stands.

findings.title: Convoluted wall being defined by the laser cutting
findings.attack: A convolution is a radial excursion of the wall; laser cutting a tube does not by itself displace the wall radially, so that alternative is not enabled as recited, and Example 1 never says which step formed the convolution.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Record which step formed the convolution in Example 1, and delete by the laser cutting from claim 90 or explain how a cut profile defines the convolution.
findings.ruling_reason: Best defence is [0147]: 'the convoluted wall (32) may be defined by the laser-cut profile ... the disclosure ... does not depend on which of these steps imparts the convolution'. That asserts the alternative but does not enable it. [0017], [0028] and [0079] define a convolution as a radial excursion of the wall measured from its mean radius. Cutting through a tube wall removes material and does not displace the wall radially, and no paragraph explains how a cut profile alone produces that excursion. [0148] (fixture 'constrains the convoluted wall to its intended wave geometry') enables the shape-setting route, and [0150] (roll-forming) enables another. Claim 90 therefore recites one alternative ('by the laser cutting') that the text does not support, and [0156] does not say which step formed the convolution of Example 1. Deleting 'by the laser cutting' from claim 90 needs no new matter. Stating the Example 1 forming step needs the inventor.

findings.title: Inverted arrangement and deflation-only purge disclosed and excluded by claim 1
findings.attack: The ring-on-poppet arrangement and deflation-only purge are described, unclaimed and outside 'carried by the core body' and the pressure-differential purge state; dedicated or argued as deliberately excluded.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Counsel to decide whether to claim on [0117] and [0067] or leave unclaimed.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate. The deflation-only purge of [0067] is raised, with the same claims and the same remedy, in F-33-4, and the inverted skirt-on-poppet arrangement of [0117] in F-33-9. Both are ruled there.

findings.title: NiTi-derived ranges claimed for every material and geometry
findings.attack: The description ties the ranges to the superelastic convoluted ring and says they must be adapted for other forms; the claims, including a PEEK ring in claims 76-77, assert them for every form.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Amend [0088] and [0091] if the inventor confirms the ranges hold across materials; otherwise make the range claims depend on claims 47/73 and 11.
findings.ruling_reason: The description itself limits the ranges. [0088] gives them as 'the ranges within which the mechanism is expected to operate with a seat ring (30) of that material and wall geometry'. [0091] says 'The ranges correspond to the superelastic seat ring (30) with a convoluted wall (32). A person skilled in the art will adapt them' to polymer, resilient-metal, other-geometry and wiper-ring forms, and [0146] repeats this. Yet claims 16-17, 35, 41-43 hang from claim 1, which covers any material and geometry. Independent claim 67 (no material) and claims 76-77 (a PEEK ring) recite the NiTi-derived inner diameter and wall thickness. The drafter's reply that [0006] makes each range an operating window does not help, because [0088] ties that window to one material. On the text this is a credible Art. 84 EPC / written-description objection. The fix is either inventor confirmation that the ranges hold across materials, or re-dependency on claims 47/73 and 11.

findings.title: Result language on an unclaimed material in claims 25, 79 and 81
findings.attack: Shearing and carrying sealant film are results on a material not part of the claimed article, and 'surfaces on which sealant film accumulates' depends on use.
findings.least_narrowing_action: 'so as to shear sealant film, when present'; name the purge flow path surfaces by structure in claim 79.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate for claims 25 and 79. Claim 25 ('shears sealant film') is ruled under F-32-19, and claim 79 ('across surfaces on which sealant film accumulates') under F-33-12. For claim 81 alone the objection fails. Claim 81 is a method-of-use claim whose parent claim 79 recites 'an inflatable chamber which holds liquid sealant'. In a method of operation, a result produced by the recited step on material present in the method is a legitimate limitation, supported by [0056].

findings.title: Shears sealant film is a result to be achieved
findings.attack: The apparatus is defined by an unmeasured effect on a material outside the claim; whether a ring riding over the film infringes is unclear; against index #3's closing-stroke wiper rings, the distinguishing point is the recovering ring itself, which the claim should recite.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recast claim 25 kinematically (a portion of the ring moves across and in contact with a surface of the poppet during shape recovery) and keep the shearing effect in the description.
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 25 is a product claim that defines the ring by a result on material outside the claimed article: 'shears sealant film from that surface'. The description makes shearing a matter of degree. [0063]: the superelastic ring 'shears ... rather than riding over it', while PEEK gives a 'weaker' wipe. [0158]: the audible snap 'is not a measurement ... of the extent of the snap-back wipe'. Whether a ring that partly rides over the film infringes is therefore unclear (EPO result-to-be-achieved; proof requires used product). The drafter's best defence, a capability reading, is weakened by [0063]'s own contrast. [0124] states that the snap-back wipe 'is defined by that movement and not by its speed or force', so the kinematic recast ('moves across and in contact with a surface of the poppet during shape recovery') is fully supported and loses nothing. Keep 'shears' in method claim 80.

findings.title: The axial load path of the purge shoulder is not described and reads against the opening direction
findings.attack: The poppet opens chamber-wards, so a shoulder on the chamber side of the sealing face moves away from the sealing edge and can meet only an undescribed supply-facing ring surface further chamber-wards; the axial order of shoulder 24, edge 34, convolutions and shoulder 44 is never stated, and the retainer of [0116] appears reversed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a paragraph stating the axial order and the face contacted, taken from the prototype and the inventor sketches, and correct [0116] if it is reversed.
findings.ruling_reason: Upheld. Severity is raised because the text, as written, puts the core mechanism of claims 3, 4 and 22 into an arrangement that cannot work. [0046]: on opening, 'the poppet (40) moves ... towards the chamber side, lifting the sealing face (42) from the sealing edge (34)'. So the sealing edge lies on the supply side of the sealing face. [0038], [0052] and claim 3 place the purge shoulder 'on the chamber side of the sealing face'. A shoulder there moves away from the seat ring as the poppet opens, and could bear on it only through a supply-facing ring surface lying further chamber-wards. No paragraph or figure description discloses such a surface. [0116] puts the retainer contact at 'the chamber-side end of the seat ring ... remote from the sealing edge', which places the sealing edge at the supply-side end, and that is hard to reconcile with [0046]. The axial order of internal shoulder (24), sealing edge (34), convolutions (32a, 32b) and purge shoulder (44) is never stated. As drafted, claim 3 faces a credible support and enablement objection, and the ordering must come from the inventor's sketches or prototype before filing, because it cannot be added afterwards.

findings.title: The worked-example dimensions do not fit together geometrically
findings.attack: With a mean radius of about 1.25 mm, a 0.12 mm outward crest gives about 2.94 mm outer diameter, which cannot enter a bore sized for 0.03 mm interference on 2.7 mm without an undisclosed relief; an inward trough gives about 2.06 mm inner diameter against an unstated stem diameter.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State the direction of the convolutions, any bore relief over the convoluted length, and the diameter of the poppet stem.
findings.ruling_reason: Upheld as a disclosure gap. The premise that the dimensions cannot fit is overstated, but the gap is real. The arithmetic is right: [0089] inner diameter 2.3 mm, wall 0.20 mm and outer diameter 2.7 mm give a mean radius of 1.25 mm. A 0.12 mm outward crest gives an outer diameter of about 2.94 mm, which cannot enter a bore sized for 0.03 mm interference on 2.7 mm ([0036]) unless the bore is relieved over the convoluted length. An inward trough gives about 2.06 mm at the trough. The values are consistent with inward convolutions and a stem under about 2.06 mm, or with a relieved bore. [0036] ('not in interference with the core body bore') hints at a relief but gives no dimension. The package states neither the convolution direction, nor any bore relief, nor the diameter of the poppet stem (41). Claim 78 recites the exact values, and filling this after filing would be new matter. Related tension: [0040] and FIG. 3 describe outward deflection opening a gap at the outer surface, which is coherent only on the [0103] reading.

findings.title: Numeral format drift, registry mismatches and claim 100 preamble
findings.attack: Numerals unbracketed in [0030]-[0041] and bracketed thereafter; claim 58 uses (30) where the description uses 730; registry rows 12, 32, 62, 64 do not match the figure instructions; claims 100-102 recite assembly under a seat-ring manufacturing preamble.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Bracket numerals uniformly; claim 58 '(30, 730)'; correct the registry rows; retitle claims 100-102 as a method of manufacturing a valve core.
findings.ruling_reason: Verified on the text. [0030]-[0041] use unbracketed numerals ('seat ring 30'), while [0042] onwards brackets them. Claim 58 recites 'deflectable ring element (30)', but the stem-carried ring of [0138] and claim 62 is 730. Claims 100-102 add a step of pressing into a core body, which lies outside a 'method of manufacturing a seat ring' preamble (claim 90). The registry rows 12, 32, 62 and 64 are not in the review package, so that part could not be checked here and is left to the registry check. Formal and low, fixable in place.

findings.title: Independent claims require a normal-open state that the description itself says may be absent
findings.attack: [0051] discloses setting the over-travel threshold close to the crack pressure so the purge state is reached on substantially every opening with a single-rate spring; every independent claim requires a normal-open state with an over-travel threshold higher than the crack pressure, so that cheaper variant is outside all of them.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim (valve core and method) reciting the closed state and the purge state only, the ring deflected when the poppet is displaced beyond a first displacement and recovering when the differential falls, supported by [0051], [0014], [0065]; keep claim 1 as the three-state claim.
findings.ruling_reason: Upheld. Severity is corrected because the premise is partly overstated. [0051] as written keeps a short normal stroke and a threshold 'close to' but still above the crack pressure, and claim 40 covers the single-rate spring. The embodiment literally described is therefore inside claim 1. The real escape is the variant [0051] points to ('purge state ... reached on substantially every opening'): a deflecting formation that meets the ring at the crack pressure, so there is no normal-open state and no threshold higher than the crack pressure, as claims 1, 58 and 79 require. An independent claim reciting only the closed and purge states, with the three-state claim kept as the fallback, is supported by [0014], [0051] and [0065], and costs nothing in support. Counsel should weigh novelty: the normal-stroke/over-travel sequence is part of what distinguishes index #13, #14 and #16.

findings.title: Normal-open state requires the ring 'in its at-rest form': escaped by light contact or by a ring-stiffness threshold
findings.attack: A deflecting formation that touches and slightly loads the ring during the normal stroke, without opening the purge gap, removes the 'at-rest form' of the normal-open state, so claims 1, 58 and 79 are not met. The ring-stiffness threshold of [0122] (initial elastic rise before the plateau), and [0050], describe exactly this, making claim 40 arguably fall outside claim 1. [0118] ('not touched') supports the narrow construction. Proof needs micro-CT or sectioning under pressure.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete 'the deflectable ring element is in its at-rest form and' from the normal-open state of claims 1, 58 and 79, keeping 'the purge gap is closed' ([0102]). Add a sentence to [0118] and [0122] that the formation may contact and elastically load the ring below the threshold without opening the purge gap, and amend 'is not touched' to 'is not deflected so as to open the purge gap'. Broadening only.
findings.ruling_reason: The normal-open state of claims 1, 58 and 79 requires 'the deflectable ring element is in its at-rest form'. [0010] ('at rest when it is not deflected by the purge shoulder'), [0047] ('not loaded ... retains its at-rest form') and [0118] ('the deflectable ring element is not touched') support a narrow reading, which a light-contact formation escapes. The finding also exposes an internal conflict. Under claim 40 and [0122], with a single-rate spring and the threshold set by ring stiffness, the formation must load the ring through its 'initial elastic rise' while the pressure differential is still below the threshold, that is, in the normal-open state. Claim 40 therefore sits uneasily with claim 1. Deleting 'the deflectable ring element is in its at-rest form and' from the normal-open state is broadening and is supported by [0043] and [0102] ('purge gap ... closed in ... the normal-open state'). Amending [0118] and [0122] needs inventor confirmation that sub-threshold contact is within the conception.

findings.title: Over-travel by mechanical depression is disclosed but no independent claim covers it
findings.attack: A Schrader-pattern core, or a Presta adaptor with a depressor, uses a stiff single-rate spring and reaches over-travel only by depression. Claim 79's 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold' is never performed. Against claims 1 and 58 the defendant uses [0058] and [0088] (threshold within the device's pressure range) and claim 46's 'additionally' to require a pressure-driven purge in use, forcing the patentee to over-pressurise seized product beyond its rating.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite the purge state in claims 1 and 58 as reached when the pressure differential exceeds the over-travel threshold or when the poppet is mechanically depressed beyond the normal stroke, or add a parallel independent claim. Add a method claim with depressor-induced or hand-induced over-travel ([0066], [0067], [0137]).
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-33-4: same escape (over-travel by a depressor, [0066] and [0137]), same claims (1, 58, 79, 46) and an equivalent remedy. The claim 46 'additionally' and [0058] construction points raised here are carried in the ruling on F-33-4.

findings.title: Purge state tied to the pressure differential; depressor-actuated and deflation-only purges escape
findings.attack: Claim 1 places the purge state 'at a pressure differential exceeding the over-travel threshold' and claim 79 requires 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold'; [0066] discloses over-travel by a pump-head depressor 'whatever the pressure differential' and [0067] a deflation-only purge, so a Schrader-style depressor product or a deflation-purge product infringes no independent claim.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate the purge state in an independent claim by poppet position ('when the poppet is displaced beyond the normal stroke into over-travel'), with the pressure threshold, the depressor and the deflation purge as dependent alternatives; supported by [0012], [0066], [0067].
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 79 requires 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold', which a depressor-actuated purge never performs. [0066] discloses over-travel by a depressor 'whatever the pressure differential', [0137] says this is how a Schrader poppet is operated, and [0067] discloses a deflation-only purge. For claims 1 and 58 the drafter's best defence is a capability reading: any sprung poppet has some pressure at which it over-travels. The defendant answers with [0058] (threshold 'within the pressure differential that the intended inflation device produces') and with claim 46's 'additionally', which implies that a pressure-driven purge is required. Both are credible. The disclosed but unclaimed routes also invite a US dedication argument. A position-defined purge state ('poppet displaced beyond the normal stroke into over-travel'), with pressure, depressor and deflation as dependents, is supported by [0012], [0066] and [0067].

findings.title: Return spring named in every product claim; a pressure-closed poppet has none
findings.attack: Deleting the spring and closing the poppet by chamber pressure, with the over-travel threshold set by ring stiffness as in [0122], yields a product with every cleaning feature and no 'return spring'; the genus 'biasing member' at [0009] is disclosed only as springs.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite 'a biasing member' in the independent claims ([0009], [0022]) and add disclosure of a poppet biased closed by chamber-side pressure without a separate spring, threshold set by the ring, subject to inventor confirmation.
findings.ruling_reason: Claims 1, 58 and 79 require a return spring. [0022] defines 'return spring' as 'the biasing member that biases the poppet towards the closed state', and [0122] describes threshold-setting by ring stiffness only 'with a return spring (50) of a single rate'. No paragraph discloses a poppet closed by chamber pressure alone, without a biasing member, and pressure is not a 'member' even under [0009]. The escape is real only if such a product can reach a distinct crack pressure and over-travel threshold. Whether the inventor conceived a spring-less poppet, and whether it works, is outside the package. It is resolved by inventor confirmation, followed by disclosure before filing if confirmed. The wording point (species against genus) is ruled separately under F-33-19.

findings.title: Seat ring claim 67 limited to Presta-sized rings by numerical ranges in the independent claim
findings.attack: 'a seat ring inner diameter of from 2.0 mm to 2.6 mm and a seat ring wall thickness of from 0.15 mm to 0.30 mm' excludes every Schrader-pattern ring the description contemplates at [0137] and [0091], and a 2.65 mm or 0.32 mm Presta ring; the component claim is the easiest of the five to avoid.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Broaden claim 67 by dropping the ranges, resting on sealing edge, axial-to-radial conversion wall and shape recovery (optionally superelastic alloy), supported by [0034], [0078], [0084], [0091]; keep claims 16, 17, 78 as fallbacks.
findings.ruling_reason: Upheld. Severity is corrected. The ranges in claim 67 ('from 2.0 mm to 2.6 mm', 'from 0.15 mm to 0.30 mm') exclude the Schrader-scale rings of [0137] and the scaled rings of [0091]. A dimension-free ring claim (sealing edge, axial-to-radial conversion wall, shape recovery) is supported by [0034], [0078] and [0084]. The loss is confined to the stand-alone ring channel of [0141], because claims 1 and 58 do not carry the ranges. The ranges may also be doing novelty work against index #1, a NiTi wave-section ring with radial displacement. Broadening is therefore a counsel trade-off after a fresh read of #1, not a required fix. See F-32-17 on the support limits of the ranges themselves.

findings.title: 'at-rest form' required in the normal-open state; a pre-loaded ring escapes
findings.attack: A purge shoulder that touches and lightly pre-loads the ring at the end of the normal stroke without opening the gap means the ring is not 'in its at-rest form' in the normal-open state; the product behaves identically and the pre-load is below the purge gap opening so is hard to prove either way.
findings.least_narrowing_action: In the normal-open state recite only that the purge gap is closed (and the main passage open), dropping 'at-rest form' there; supported by [0018], [0043]; keep it in the closed state.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-33-2: the same 'at-rest form' limitation in the normal-open state of claims 1 and 58, the same pre-loaded-ring escape and the same deletion remedy.

findings.title: 'radial deflection' excludes an axially collapsing ring that uncovers an opening
findings.attack: [0079] concedes a wall that 'merely shortens' is outside the mechanism; a bellows-like ring that shortens axially under the shoulder and uncovers a port or lifts a lip axially has no radial deflection and escapes every independent claim.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure of a deflectable ring element whose over-travel deformation, axial or radial, uncovers the purge opening, if within the inventors' conception; otherwise accept the boundary.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-33-13. Both attack the 'radial deflection' limitation ([0020]) through a ring that deforms axially or out of plane to open a port, and both depend on the same unconfirmed conception. The axially collapsing, bellows-like variant is covered in the ruling on F-33-13.

findings.title: Disclosed actuation architectures outside claim 1: separate purge actuator and inverted arrangement
findings.attack: Claim 1 needs the ring 'carried by the core body' and the poppet to 'produce a radial deflection'; [0123] discloses a separate annular piston or diaphragm deflecting the ring while the poppet does only its normal stroke, and [0117] a skirt carried by the poppet deflected by a fixed formation; a Schrader product with a purge piston infringes nothing.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add formulations in which 'a deflecting member movable in response to the pressure differential' produces the deflection (poppet as one species) and in which the ring is carried by the core body or the poppet; supported by [0112], [0117], [0123].
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 1 requires that 'the poppet ... produces a radial deflection' and that the ring be 'carried by the core body'. The separate purge actuator of [0123] ('the poppet (40) performing only its normal stroke') does not meet the first. The inverted skirt 'carried by the poppet' of [0117] meets the second only on a strained indirect-carriage reading of [0005], since the poppet is guided by the core body, not fixed to it. Both are disclosed and unclaimed. A formulation in which a deflecting member moved in response to the pressure differential produces the deflection, and the ring is carried by the core body or the poppet, is supported by [0112], [0117] and [0123]. Counsel should check the broader deflecting-member wording against index #16 (separately moving members opening a second path).

findings.title: Manufacturing claim 90 hidden in the supplier's process and its evidence removed by electropolishing
findings.attack: 'laser cutting' and 'water quenching' are single disclosed species; [0150] discloses roll-forming, internal-pressure forming, etching of sheet and stamping which all escape, and the electropolishing of [0149] removes the heat-affected edge that would evidence laser cutting; the process is performed abroad and undetectable from the product.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate to 'cutting a profile of the seat ring from tube stock or from sheet' ([0150]); generalising the quench requires new disclosure; counsel to weigh whether claim 90 earns its examination cost.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-33-11: the same claim 90 limitations ('laser cutting', 'water quenching'), the same alternative routes ([0150]), the same point that electropolishing removes the trace ([0149]), and the same remedy.

findings.title: Manufacturing claim 90 is hidden in the factory and escaped by changing the quench or the cutting route
findings.attack: The process is performed abroad and electropolishing removes the laser trace ([0149]). Air or oil cooling escapes 'water quenching', and photochemical etching or stamping escapes 'laser cutting' ([0150]). Product-by-process protection for imports presupposes proof of the process.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete 'and then water quenching' from claim 90 (kept in claim 94). Make laser cutting one alternative for producing the profile and put it in a dependent claim ([0147], [0148], [0150]). Counsel to weigh the EPO intermediate-generalisation risk.
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 90 recites 'laser cutting a profile ... from the tube stock' and 'then water quenching'. [0148] discloses only water quenching, and [0150] discloses roll-forming, split-die forming, photochemical etching and stamping as other routes. [0149] states that electropolishing removes 'the heat-affected edge left by laser cutting', so the claimed process leaves little trace on the product, and it may be performed abroad. Moving 'water quenching' to claim 94 is literally supported by claim 94 and [0148]. The description never says the quench is optional, however, so the EPO intermediate-generalisation risk the finding flags is real, and counsel must weigh it. Reciting cutting generically with laser cutting as a dependent is supported by [0147] and [0150].

findings.title: Method claim 79 performed by the user and requires proof of sealant film on the accused surfaces
findings.attack: Every step is performed by the cyclist so the competitor is reached only by indirect infringement; 'across surfaces on which sealant film accumulates' makes infringement depend on the condition of the accused valve at the time of use and requires proof of film on those surfaces.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite 'across a surface of the deflectable ring element' ([0056]) in claim 79 and move 'on which sealant film accumulates' to a dependent claim; ensure product claims carry every structural feature the method relies on.
findings.ruling_reason: Every step of claim 79 ('coupling an inflation device', 'raising', 'removing') is the user's act, so a competitor is reached only by inducement or contributory infringement, or under UK s.60(2). 'Across surfaces on which sealant film accumulates' ties infringement to the state of the accused valve in use. [0056] names those surfaces structurally ('the outer surface of the seat ring (30) and the adjoining region of the core body bore (22)'), so 'across a surface of the deflectable ring element' is supported and removes the condition that depends on use. The film condition can move to a dependent claim.

findings.title: Only radial, in-place deformation is covered: axial flexing or bodily displacement of the ring escapes
findings.attack: A diaphragm ring that flexes out of plane to lift a lip from an axial face, or a rigid ring pushed axially off a land to uncover flutes, opens a purge path only in over-travel without any 'radial deflection' as defined in [0020]. The bodily displaced form lies near refs. #13 and #16.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If within conception, add an embodiment in which elastic out-of-plane flexure of the ring opens the purge gap, and claim 'elastic deformation of the deflectable ring element' without 'radial'. Do not claim bodily displacement unless counsel is satisfied on refs. #13 and #16.
findings.ruling_reason: On the text the escape is real. [0020] limits 'radial deflection' to in-place wall deformation, 'not a bodily displacement', and [0079] excludes a wall that 'merely shortens'. [0082], a conical disc whose flattening moves the free rim radially, is the nearest disclosure, but it still opens the gap radially. No embodiment discloses out-of-plane flexure lifting a lip from an axial face, or axial collapse uncovering a port (which also covers F-33-8). Whether these fall within the inventors' conception is outside the package. Bodily axial displacement of a rigid ring also lies near index #13 and #16, which counsel must weigh. It is resolved by inventor confirmation of an axial-flexure embodiment before filing; a claim to 'elastic deformation' without 'radial' then follows.

findings.title: Purge gap 'closed' in the closed and normal-open states; a permanent small downstream clearance escapes
findings.attack: A purge gap on the chamber side of the sealing edge ([0105]) can carry a permanent measurable clearance without leaking the tyre; such a gap is never 'closed', and [0105]'s 'sufficiently small to carry no significant flow' wording applies only to that one location, not to the generic definition at [0018].
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a generic sentence to [0018] that the purge gap is 'closed' when closed or carrying no significant flow relative to the main passage, extending [0105] to every location, and rely on it in the claims.
findings.ruling_reason: [0018] defines the purge gap generically as 'closed in the closed state and in the normal-open state'. The 'closed, or ... sufficiently small to carry no significant flow' alternative appears only for the third arrangement in [0105], so a permanent small clearance in series with the sealing edge escapes the generic definition in claims 1, 58 and 79. The text makes the point sharper. [0036] and [0053] say the rest of the seat-ring outer surface is 'not in interference' with and 'free of' the core body bore, which in the illustrated embodiment itself suggests a clearance at rest where [0040] calls the gap closed. Extending the [0105] wording into [0018] is a definitional change the drafter can make before filing, with inventor confirmation of what 'no significant flow' means for the prototype.

findings.title: Seat ring claim 67 is avoided by leaving the dimensional window, or by a wall convoluted along its whole length
findings.attack: A Schrader-scale ring, an inner diameter of 2.65 mm, a wall of 0.32 mm, a FIG. 12 wall, or a wall convoluted end to end (no 'portion of the wall free of convolutions' at which to measure under [0028]) escapes claim 67. Replacement rings outside the window are free.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a fallback measurement convention to [0028] (for example, the diameter at the sealing edge (34) where no portion is free of convolutions). Consider an independent seat-ring claim without dimensions (sealing edge for a poppet, convoluted wall, superelastic alloy), with the ranges as dependents, subject to counsel's view on ref. #1. The current claim gives up every non-Presta-scale ring.
findings.ruling_reason: [0028] measures the seat ring inner diameter and outer diameter 'at a portion of the wall free of convolutions'. For a ring convoluted end to end there is no such portion, so the inner-diameter limitation of claim 67 cannot be determined and becomes an escape as well as a clarity point. A fallback convention (for example, at the sealing edge (34)) is a definition the drafter can add before filing. The broader proposal for a dimension-free ring claim is ruled under F-33-6.

findings.title: Separate purge actuator and inverted arrangement escape 'the poppet ... produces a radial deflection' and 'carried by the core body'
findings.attack: With the purge actuator of [0123] the poppet performs only its normal stroke, so no purge state as claimed exists. With the inverted skirt-on-poppet arrangement of [0117], 'carried by the core body' depends on a contested indirect-carriage reading of [0005].
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite the deflection as produced by a deflecting formation moved by the poppet in over-travel or by a purge actuator responsive to the pressure differential exceeding the over-travel threshold ([0123]), and the ring as carried by the core body or by the poppet ([0117]).
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-33-9: the same purge actuator ([0123]) and inverted arrangement ([0117]), the same limitations ('the poppet ... produces', 'carried by the core body') and an equivalent remedy.

findings.title: Shape recovery 'to its at-rest form' and tied to the over-travel threshold
findings.attack: [0099] admits residual set after many cycles; a competitor shows its cycled ring does not return 'to' the at-rest form, and a ring whose gap closes only below the crack pressure argues it does not close 'when the pressure differential falls below the over-travel threshold'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite 'shape recovery towards its at-rest form and closing the purge gap when the pressure differential falls', tracking [0013] and [0014].
findings.ruling_reason: Claims 1, 58, 67 and 79 recite shape recovery 'to its at-rest form' and closing 'when the pressure differential falls below the over-travel threshold'. [0013] and [0014] use 'towards its at-rest shape/form', and [0099] concedes 'residual set of the ring element after many cycles', so a cycled ring may not return exactly to its at-rest form. [0074] acknowledges transformation hysteresis, and [0122] notes that the threshold depends on temperature, which supports the argument that the gap closes below the threshold rather than on reaching it. The drafter can point to [0060] and [0098] ('to its at-rest form'), but the description is inconsistent and the claim takes the narrow word. The [0014] wording ('towards', 'when the pressure differential falls') is supported and costs nothing.

findings.title: Supply of seat ring, poppet and return spring as a kit, or of core parts to a stem maker, avoids claim 1
findings.attack: Claim 1 requires 'a core body (20)'. A matched kit of ring, poppet and spring for assembly into someone else's core body, or parts shipped to a stem maker, is not a direct infringement. Indirect infringement needs knowledge, and claim 67 catches only rings inside its window.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a kit claim: deflectable ring element, poppet with sealing face and deflecting formation, and return spring, matched so that on assembly the closed, normal-open and purge states of claim 1 result ([0141], FIG. 5).
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 1 requires a core body (20), and claim 67 covers the ring only inside its dimensional window. A matched ring, poppet and spring supplied without a core body ([0141], [0180], FIG. 5) is at most an indirect infringement, which needs knowledge. [0141] discloses the kit 'matched so that, when assembled into the core body (20), the purge shoulder (44) is spaced ... throughout the normal stroke and bears ... only in over-travel, and the purge gap (60) is closed in the closed state and the normal-open state', which supports a kit claim directly. For the kit claim's states, the fixes from F-33-2 and F-33-4 should be adopted.

findings.title: 'return spring' is the species; the package defines the genus 'biasing member'
findings.attack: A non-spring bias invites the argument that the plain meaning of 'spring' prevails over [0022].
findings.least_narrowing_action: Use 'a biasing member (50)' in the independent claims ([0009], [0022]).
findings.ruling_reason: [0022] defines 'return spring' as 'the biasing member that biases the poppet', but [0009] calls the return spring 'the species described in detail' of the genus 'biasing member'. The two paragraphs give opposing grounds for a plain-meaning argument that 'spring' excludes a non-spring bias. Reciting 'a biasing member (50)' in the independent claims is supported by [0009] and [0022] and costs nothing. Low. See F-33-5 for the spring-less poppet, which this wording does not cover.

findings.title: 'separate from the main passage' invites a construction fight where the flows merge
findings.attack: Where the purge flow runs along the poppet stem ([0105]), the defendant argues that the purge path is not 'separate' from the main passage.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite the purge gap as a flow path distinct from the main passage and opened only by the radial deflection, locating the separation at the gap ([0019], [0045], [0102]).
findings.ruling_reason: The text already answers it. [0019] states that the main passage and purge gap 'are different flow paths: the main passage is opened by lifting of the sealing face ... whereas the purge gap is opened only by radial deflection'. [0043] uses 'separate' in the same sense. [0105] addresses exactly the stem-path case the finding raises: the clearance 'remains a flow path distinct from the main passage (64)'. Merging downstream in the chamber ([0056]) is described and does not defeat separateness as defined. Harmonising 'separate' to 'distinct' is optional polish.

findings.title: Method of operating claim 79 is performed by the end user
findings.attack: The cyclist is the direct infringer. A competitor is liable only for inducement or contributory infringement (knowledge and intent), or under UK s.60(2), and the claim is confined by [0025] to bicycle chambers holding sealant.
findings.least_narrowing_action: No change required. Keep the product claims free of in-use requirements, and carry the fixes for F-33-1 and F-33-2 into claim 79.
findings.ruling_reason: Upheld on its second point only; the user-infringer point duplicates F-33-12. [0025] defines 'inflatable chamber' as the volume 'of a bicycle inner tube or of a tubeless bicycle tyre set-up'. That lexicography confines claim 79, the 'for an inflatable chamber' preamble of claim 58, and claim 64 to bicycles. It contradicts [0139], which applies the mechanism 'to inflation valves for other inflatable chambers that hold liquid sealant', and it leaves claim 85 adding nothing. Recasting [0025] as an example ('for example a bicycle inner tube ...') removes the confinement. Low, because the bicycle application is the one built and tested.

findings.title: Product claim 25 recites a result in use: 'shears sealant film'
findings.attack: An unused core has no film to shear, so proof needs used product and evidence of shearing that the package concedes is not separately measured.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite the movement alone ('moves across a surface of the poppet'), which [0124] makes definitive, and keep 'shears sealant film' in method claim 80.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-32-19: the same result language in claim 25 ('shears sealant film'), the same proof problem ([0158]) and the same kinematic remedy resting on [0124].

findings.title: Claim 67 scores 3 for design-around resistance
findings.attack: A Schrader-scale ring, a ring just outside either range, a FIG. 12 wall, or a wall with no convolution-free portion for the [0028] measurement escapes, leaving the replacement-seat-ring channel of [0141] free.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a fallback measurement convention to [0028]. Consider an independent seat-ring claim without dimensions (sealing edge for a poppet, convoluted wall, superelastic alloy) with the ranges as dependents, subject to counsel's view on index #1.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate. It is a scoring restatement of F-33-15 (the [0028] measurement convention and the dimensional window of claim 67) and F-33-6 (the dimension-free ring claim, subject to index #1), with the same remedies.

findings.title: Claim 90 scores 2 for design-around resistance and 2 for detectability
findings.attack: Changing the quench medium or cutting route escapes 'laser cutting' and 'then water quenching'. The process runs abroad and electropolishing removes its trace ([0149]), so the claim adds almost no moat.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete 'and then water quenching' (kept in claim 94) and recite laser cutting as one alternative with a dependent claim ([0147], [0148], [0150]). Counsel to weigh the EPO intermediate-generalisation risk.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate. It is a scoring restatement of F-33-11 on claim 90 ('laser cutting', 'then water quenching', the trace removed by electropolishing per [0149]), with an identical remedy.

findings.title: Claims 1 and 58 score 5 for design-around resistance: four disclosed escape architectures are unclaimed
findings.attack: The description discloses the two-state single-rate-spring variant ([0051]), the depressor-actuated purge ([0066]), the separate purge actuator ([0123]) and the inverted ring-on-poppet arrangement ([0117]); none is inside an independent claim, which requires a normal-open state, a return spring and poppet-produced radial deflection.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim to the closed and purge states only, purge state defined by displacement of a deflecting member beyond a first displacement, ring carried by the core body or the poppet, and 'a biasing member' for the spring; supported by [0009], [0022], [0051], [0066], [0112], [0117], [0123].
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate. It aggregates escapes ruled individually: the two-state variant of [0051] (F-33-1), the depressor-actuated purge of [0066] (F-33-4), the separate purge actuator of [0123] and the inverted arrangement of [0117] (F-33-9), and 'biasing member' (F-33-19, F-33-5). The remedies proposed are the union of those rulings.

findings.title: Method claim 79 scores 4 for detectability and 4 for evidentiary ease
findings.attack: Every step is the user's act; proof of 'an air purge ... across surfaces on which sealant film accumulates' needs the accused valve after use with sealant, a bench rig and evidence that the user's pump exceeded the threshold, which [0179] concedes hand pumps and CO2 devices may not.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite 'across a surface of the deflectable ring element' ([0056]) in place of the sealant-film condition; carry every structural precondition into claims 1 and 58; keep claim 79 as the inducement vehicle.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-33-12: claim 79 is performed by the user and carries the sealant-film condition, with the same [0056] remedy. The added point that proof depends on the user's pump exceeding the threshold ([0179]) follows from the pressure-defined purge state and is answered by the position-defined formulation ruled under F-33-4.

findings.title: Seat ring claim 67 scores 3 for design-around resistance because of numerical ranges and the convoluted-wall limitation
findings.attack: 'a seat ring inner diameter of from 2.0 mm to 2.6 mm and a seat ring wall thickness of from 0.15 mm to 0.30 mm' and 'a convoluted wall (32)' exclude every Schrader-pattern ring, any Presta ring marginally outside the ranges, and the frustoconical, slotted and cellular walls of [0081]; an aftermarket ring supplier avoids the only component claim at no engineering cost.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Broaden claim 67 to the sealing edge, the axial-to-radial conversion wall (claim 10 wording, [0078]) and shape recovery, adding the superelastic alloy of claim 73 if novelty needs it; keep ranges and convoluted wall as dependents.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-33-6: the same ranges in claim 67 and the same Schrader-scale and marginal-range escapes. Its proposal to recite the axial-to-radial conversion wall in place of 'convoluted wall' ([0078], [0081]) is already the remedy in F-33-6, where it is ruled together with the index #1 caveat.

findings.title: Claim 79 scores 4 for design-around resistance
findings.attack: An adaptor with a depressor produces over-travel without 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold'; a pump below the threshold produces no purge at all.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a method claim with over-travel produced by mechanical depression during coupling ([0066], [0067]).
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 79 requires 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold'. A method in which a depressor in the head or adaptor pushes the poppet into over-travel 'whatever the pressure differential' ([0066]) does not perform that step. Claim 46 covers the depressor only as a product feature, and claim 88 covers pressing only during deflation. Best defence: claim 79 still reads where the pump also exceeds the threshold. That does not reach a depressor used with a low-pressure device. A method claim can be added from [0066]/[0067] without new matter. Overlaps F-36-16, which is the broader independent-claim version.

findings.title: Load path of the purge shoulder and through-route of the purge flow past the retention band not stated for the illustrated embodiment
findings.attack: The description never states which end of the seat ring carries the sealing edge relative to the internal shoulder, which ring surface the purge shoulder (on the chamber side of the sealing face, moving in the opening direction) bears on, or how gas in the annular outer-surface purge gap passes the interference band that seats the ring against the internal shoulder; the registry's flag 3 concedes the FIG. 6 convention is a drafting assumption, so sufficiency and clarity of claim 1's through-flow for the FIG. 1 embodiment are exposed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0034], [0038] and [0056] a plain statement of the axial arrangement and of the route by which the purge flow enters the annular purge gap at the supply side and leaves at the chamber side (past the free end and the freed region, or via purge ports 262 or flutes 362), taken from the inventor's sketches.
findings.ruling_reason: The text does not give the axial arrangement or the purge route for the FIG. 1 embodiment. [0079] puts the sealing edge at the end opposite the internal shoulder. [0116] makes the chamber-side end of the ring 'remote from the sealing edge', so the internal shoulder and the interference band ([0036], [0053]) sit at the chamber-side end, which is the end the purge gas must leave by ([0056], [0059]). No paragraph says how gas in the outer-surface gap passes that band. The mechanism also does not cohere as described: [0040] and [0053] place the gap at the outer surface, closed at rest and opened when the surface 'moves away from' the bore, yet [0020], [0053] and [0093] (and FIG. 3 in the plan) give the illustrated deflection as outward, which moves the outer surface towards the bore. [0103] concedes that this location needs inward movement. The figure plan (FIG. 6) calls the band convention a drawing convention 'adopted to reconcile' the disclosure, not something taken from the inventor. Best defence: claim 1 is generic, and the third arrangement ([0105], inner-surface gap opened by outward deflection) is coherent and supports it. That saves claim 1's scope, but not the enablement of the illustrated embodiment, and claims 4, 30 and 21 read directly on it. Only the inventor's sketches can resolve this, so it needs an answer at the gate, not a drafting assumption.

findings.title: No drawings exist: the package holds a figure plan that contains internal working references
findings.attack: The description relies on FIGs. 1-15, but the package holds only a figure plan and draftsperson instructions. Filing without drawings risks re-dating (EPC R. 56) or loss of the figure references, and the US requires drawings where necessary (35 USC 113). The plan text contains internal references ('01 Q22', 'DA-7', 'Assumption A2 in Prompt 20') that must not be filed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Produce FIGs. 1-15 from registry.md (after F-36-1 for FIGs. 1, 3, 6 and 10), complete the deferred numeral cross-check, add a Brief Description of the Drawings, and exclude all figure-plan working text from the filing.
findings.ruling_reason: The package holds only figures.md, a 'Figure Plan' that expressly says no inventor image has been seen and that FIGs. 2 and 4–15 are new. The description relies on drawings throughout ([0030], [0053], [0081], [0093], [0109], [0120], [0137]). The plan text carries internal working references ('01 Q22', 'DA-7, DA-23, DA-24', 'Prompt 16', '14.md'), which must not be filed. Without drawings, US 35 USC 113 is engaged and the EP figure references are exposed. There is also no Brief Description of the Drawings. The FIG. 1, 3 and 6 geometry depends on F-36-1 being resolved first.

findings.title: Wipe-only embodiment of [0065] has no claim family
findings.attack: [0065] discloses cleaning 'by the snap-back wipe alone, the deflectable ring element being sealed at its periphery so that no inflation gas flows past it'; claim 25 depends on claim 1 which requires the purge gap and purge flow path, so a sealed-periphery deflectable seat ring that snaps back across the sealing face infringes nothing while getting the benefit [0167] attributes to the wiped surfaces.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent valve core claim to the deflectable ring element carrying the sealing edge, deflected by the poppet in over-travel and moving across the sealing face on shape recovery, without the purge gap (purge gap dependent), plus a corresponding method claim and a figure of the sealed-periphery form; supported by [0061], [0065], [0092], FIG. 4.
findings.ruling_reason: [0065] discloses the wipe-only form ('sealed at its periphery so that no inflation gas flows past it'), and [0061], [0092] and [0124] describe the wipe independently of any flow. Every product and method independent claim (1, 58, 79) requires the purge gap and purge flow path, so claims 25 and 80 cannot reach a sealed-periphery ring. Best defence: a claim without the purge gap moves closer to closing-stroke wipers (INDEX #3 US 4,719,938; #7 US 6,006,954). That is a reason to draft it with care, not a reason to leave it unclaimed. Severity corrected to medium: this is a design-around gap in claim coverage that existing text can close, not a rejection of any pending claim. A drawing of the sealed-periphery form would help, but it is not needed for claim support.

findings.title: 'Inflatable chamber' is defined as bicycle-only; sealant-filled e-scooter, motorcycle and other tyres are left out
findings.attack: The [0025] definition confines claims 58 and 79 to bicycle chambers, so an e-scooter or motorcycle tubeless valve with the mechanism argues non-infringement. [0139] gives only a general sentence as basis for later amendment.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Redefine the inflatable chamber as any tyre or inner tube inflated through the valve and holding liquid sealant, with bicycle chambers as the tested example, and name the other contemplated chambers.
findings.ruling_reason: [0025] defines 'inflatable chamber' as the volume 'of a bicycle inner tube or of a tubeless bicycle tyre set-up', and [0001] applies that definition to the claims, so claim 79 ('an inflatable chamber which holds liquid sealant') is confined to bicycle chambers. In claim 58 the phrase is a statement of purpose, but its scope is still read through the definition. The only basis for a wider reading is the general sentence in [0139]. The definition can be widened on the strength of [0139] alone. Naming other chambers (e-scooter, motorcycle) needs the inventor to confirm them.

findings.title: Behaviour on top-up inflation is not described
findings.attack: Every tested event ran from fully deflated to 6 bar; on a top-up from riding pressure the differential across the open poppet is the flow-induced drop, not the gauge pressure, and the package does not say whether the 3.5 bar threshold is reached on a floor-pump stroke into a pressurised chamber, while [0068] states the cleaning actions occur 'once per inflation event'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a paragraph after [0069] stating whether and on what basis the purge state is reached on top-up inflation, and that the tested event is inflation from fully deflated; if unknown, say so in the manner of [0165].
findings.ruling_reason: The enablement objection is answered in part. [0069] and [0179] already say that whether an inflation event reaches the purge state 'depends on the pressure differential that the inflation device produces', and [0068] limits 'once per inflation event' to an event 'that reaches the purge state' and names the tested event as 'from fully deflated to 6 bar'. Claims 79 and 87 are conditional on exceeding the threshold. What remains is a fact outside the package: whether a floor-pump top-up from riding pressure reaches a 3.5 bar differential across the poppet ([0011]). The inventor's knowledge or a test would resolve it. If the answer is no, the technical effect relied on for inventive step is narrower than [0064] implies. Severity corrected to low, because no claim is at risk on the text.

findings.title: Claimed and disclosed features without a figure
findings.attack: Claims 24, 28, 31, 32, 45 and 46, and the unclaimed retainer/sleeve, conical disc, purge actuator, inverted arrangement, wiping land, helical wipe and wipe-only forms appear in no figure; 37 CFR 1.83(a) requires claimed features to be shown and a post-filing figure cannot add matter, and at the EPO and UK an undrawn alternative is the first called an unsupported generalisation.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add schematic partial sections in the style of FIGs. 11–14 for the claimed features at least and for the wipe-only and purge-actuator forms; the description already gives the structure.
findings.ruling_reason: Checked against the figure plan: none of FIGs. 1–15 shows the integral flexure (claim 24, [0096]), the second return formation (claim 28, [0099]), the inner-surface purge gap (claim 31, [0105]), the over-travel stop (claim 45, [0049]) or the depressor (claim 46, [0066]; FIG. 7 is only a state diagram). Claim 32's openings are only arguably shown in FIG. 12B/12C, which the plan draws as conversion geometries and not as purge openings. 37 CFR 1.83(a) applies. The EPO/UK part of the attack is overstated: support under Art. 84 comes from the description, and [0096], [0099], [0105], [0049] and [0066] describe these features in words. Medium stands on the US point. The figures can be drawn from the existing text.

findings.title: How the band-limited interference fit is made is not disclosed
findings.attack: Claim 21 and four paragraphs recite an interference over an axial band with the remainder clear, but none says whether that is by a relief in the bore, a reduced outer diameter on the ring's free portion, or a step, and the ring is drawn from plain 2.7 mm tube; the registry's flag 3 concedes the convention is a drafting assumption.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add one sentence at [0036] stating the means (bore relief, ring relief, or both) and, if known, the axial length of the band, after inventor confirmation.
findings.ruling_reason: As an enablement point this fails. A skilled person makes a fit that interferes only over an axial band by ordinary means, relieving the bore or the ring, and [0033] and [0151] state that the core body is turned 'by ordinary machining'. Claim 21 recites a result that a turner achieves routinely. The real defect is how purge gas passes that band, and whether the convolution itself interferes. That is F-36-1, upheld, and is dealt with there. If the inventor's answer to F-36-1 names the means, it can go in [0036] in the same fix.

findings.title: No claims to non-bicycle sealant-holding chambers, to the kit, or to the inflation system with a depressor head
findings.attack: Claims 64–66 are limited to bicycle chambers; [0139] extends the mechanism to other sealant-holding chambers, [0141] discloses the seat ring kit and [0066] the depressor head or adaptor, none of which is claimed and none of which can be added after filing.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a chamber claim generic to an inflatable chamber holding liquid sealant with bicycle forms dependent, a kit claim per [0141], and an inflation system claim (valve plus device head or adaptor with a depressor sized to move the poppet into over-travel) per [0066].
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 64 is limited to 'a bicycle inner tube or a tubeless bicycle tyre set-up', and no claim covers the kit of [0141] (seat ring, poppet and two-stage return spring matched for spacing) or the valve plus depressor head or adaptor of [0066]. Claim 46 recites only that the poppet 'is additionally movable' by a depressor. The premise that these claims cannot be added after filing is overstated: claims supported by [0066] and [0141] can be added in prosecution, subject in the EPO to Rule 137(5). They are still cheaper and safer to include now. The generic-chamber part overlaps F-36-4 and depends on [0139].

findings.title: No embodiment opens the purge path by out-of-plane (axial) flexure of the ring
findings.attack: A diaphragm ring flexing axially to lift a lip opens a purge path only in over-travel and escapes every claim reciting 'radial deflection'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If within conception, add the embodiment and a generic statement that the elastic deformation opening the purge gap may be radial or axial.
findings.ruling_reason: The text answers only part of this. The conical annular disc in [0082] flattens under axial load, but its rim moves radially and [0020] defines radial deflection. No paragraph discloses a diaphragm lifting a lip axially to open the purge path. Whether that form is within the inventor's conception is a fact outside the package. The inventor should be asked at the gate whether an axially flexing element opening a purge path only in over-travel was conceived; nothing may be added otherwise.

findings.title: No embodiment purges from first lift (zero normal stroke)
findings.attack: Every independent claim requires a normal-open state. A product purging from first lift has none, and [0051] discloses only a short normal stroke, so there is no basis for a claim family without it.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If within conception, add an embodiment with the purge gap opening as the poppet lifts (single-rate spring, no normal stroke) and an independent claim without the normal-open state, with counsel weighing index #14 and #16.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct on the text: claims 1, 58 and 79 all require a normal-open state, and [0051] discloses only a short normal stroke with the threshold 'close to the crack pressure' ('substantially every opening'), not purging from first lift. Whether zero-stroke purging was conceived is for the inventor. The normal-open/over-travel sequence is also part of what separates the claims from INDEX #13 (US 4,408,632) and #16 (US 8,043,186), so counsel must weigh any claim without it against those references. Resolved by the inventor's confirmation, then counsel's judgement.

findings.title: No generic definition of a 'closed' purge gap and no tolerance on 'at-rest form'
findings.attack: [0018] says the purge gap is 'closed' and [0105] gives the 'no significant flow' test for one location only; claims recite recovery 'to its at-rest form' while [0013] says 'towards' and [0099] admits residual set; strict construction gives two escapes and support for a cure at one location only.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0018] that the purge gap is closed when closed or carrying no significant flow relative to the main passage, for every location, and to [0013] that shape recovery is return towards the at-rest form sufficient to close the purge gap, residual set notwithstanding.
findings.ruling_reason: Claims 1, 58, 67 and 79 recite shape recovery 'to its at-rest form', but [0013], [0014] and [0071] say 'towards', and [0099] admits residual set. A defendant whose ring keeps some set argues the claim is not met. Only the third arrangement ([0105]) gives a 'no significant flow' test for 'closed'; [0018] and [0102] have none, and metal-on-metal closure always leaks slightly. Best defence: [0013] defines shape recovery as 'return towards its at-rest shape', which a court would read into the claim term. The literal wording 'to its at-rest form' still invites the argument. The 'towards' amendment needs no new disclosure. A general 'closed' test for every location is a new definition and should go in now.

findings.title: No ranges for the normal stroke, the rest clearance of the purge shoulder, or the spring-stage rate ratio
findings.attack: The normal stroke is a single value (0.6 mm), the rest clearance has no value and the second-stage rate is only 'higher'; the parameters a competitor's core will differ in have no numeric fallback, and [0088] supports only a qualitative amendment.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add ranges for the normal stroke, the rest clearance (at least the normal stroke plus a margin) and the ratio of second to first spring-stage rate, bracketing the tested values, as ranges within which the mechanism is expected to operate in the manner of [0006] and [0088].
findings.ruling_reason: Correct on the text: [0046] and [0090] give the normal stroke only as 0.6 mm, the rest clearance of the purge shoulder has no value, and [0022] and [0039] say only that the second stage is 'higher'. Best defence: [0088] states the governing relationship ('spaced from the deflectable ring element by at least the normal stroke at rest'), which gives a qualitative fallback. Severity corrected to low: no pending claim depends on these ranges, and numeric ranges may be added only if the inventor supplies them. [0006] does not permit the team to choose them.

findings.title: Over-travel by a depressor has no geometry or control logic
findings.attack: There is no relation between depressor travel, normal stroke and over-travel distance, and no account of how a Schrader core, whose pin every head depresses, keeps a normal-open state. The Schrader and adaptor variants, and any claim built on [0066], are exposed on enablement and support.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the depressor geometry (travel exceeding the normal stroke plus a stated fraction of the over-travel distance) and the Schrader variant's operating sequence.
findings.ruling_reason: Mostly rejected for claim 46: [0066] says the depressor 'pushes the poppet beyond the normal stroke into over-travel', and with [0090] (normal stroke 0.6 mm, over-travel 0.5 mm) a skilled person can set the depressor travel without further guidance. The Schrader point survives. [0137] says the Schrader poppet 'may be depressed by the head of the inflation device', but nothing explains how claim 57's pressure-driven normal-open state coexists with a standard head that always depresses the pin. Severity corrected to low, confined to the Schrader operating sequence, which the inventor should confirm.

findings.title: The cheapest competitor combination is disclosed only by a blanket combination statement
findings.attack: A moulded polymer core body with an integral flexure, a single-rate spring with a stiffness-set threshold, and moulded flutes is the lowest-cost competitor product. The [0143] blanket statement is weak EPO basis for selecting that combination from several lists.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a written prophetic embodiment of this combination, including how the threshold is set without a second spring stage.
findings.ruling_reason: The combination already has direct basis.
