[0143] discloses each alternative 'in combination with each of the others', and the claims as filed chain it: claim 40 (single-rate spring, threshold set by ring stiffness, [0122]) depends on claims 1–35, which include claim 34 (flutes, [0110]), which in turn depends on claims 1–33, which include claim 24 (integral flexure in a resilient-polymer core body, [0096]). Moulding is disclosed at [0096] and [0131]. [0122] explains how the threshold is set without a second stage. The EPO treats original claim dependencies as disclosure. Caution for F-37-1: that basis is kept only if the EP and UK claim sets keep their multiple dependencies.

findings.title: The package contradicts itself on whether the ring is touched below the over-travel threshold
findings.attack: [0118] says the ring is 'not touched' below the threshold, while [0122] sets the threshold by the force to deflect the ring after an initial elastic rise, which requires contact below it. Claim 40 read with claim 1's normal-open 'at-rest form' lacks support and clarity, and [0118] fixes a narrow construction.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add control logic that the formation may contact and elastically load the ring below the threshold with the purge gap still closed, amend [0118] to 'is not deflected so as to open the purge gap', and align claim 1 as in F-33-1.
findings.ruling_reason: The tension is real. [0118] says that below the threshold 'the deflectable ring element is not touched'. [0122] sets the threshold by the force needed to deflect the ring along a plateau 'after an initial elastic rise', and [0050] has the ring contribute 'once the purge shoulder bears on' it. With a single-rate spring (claim 40), contact and elastic loading therefore happen below the threshold, while claim 1's normal-open state requires the ring 'in its at-rest form', and [0010] treats 'at rest' as 'not deflected by the purge shoulder'. Claim 40 read with claim 1 is exposed on clarity and support. Rewording [0118] ('not deflected so as to open the purge gap') needs no new disclosure. The claim 1 alignment should be coordinated with F-33-1.

findings.title: Two-state, depressor-actuated and deflation-only operating modes have no independent claim
findings.attack: [0051] (threshold at the crack pressure, single-rate spring), [0066] (depressor over-travel whatever the differential) and [0067] (deflation-only purge) are each disclosed as embodiments and each is outside every independent claim, which require the three-state sequence driven by the pressure differential.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim defining the purge state by poppet displacement beyond a first displacement with the pressure threshold, the depressor and the deflation purge as dependent alternatives; supported by [0012], [0051], [0066], [0067].
findings.ruling_reason: Each of these modes is disclosed and each falls outside claims 1, 58 and 79, which require the three states driven by the pressure differential: the near-two-state form of [0051] (single rate), depressor over-travel 'whatever the pressure differential' in [0066], and deflation-only purging in [0067] ('each inflation event using the normal stroke alone'). Claim 88 depends on claim 79, so it does not cover deflation-only purging. An independent claim that defines the purge state by poppet displacement beyond the normal stroke is supported by [0012], [0066] and [0067] without new matter. It would sit closer to INDEX #13 and #14, and counsel should weigh that. Overlaps F-35-6.

findings.title: Any test data the inventors hold beyond Example 1 should be added before filing
findings.attack: Durability, cold performance and the PEEK and wiper variants are where inventive step and plausibility will be argued; data held but not filed carries less weight later.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Ask whether further results exist (including P-1 to P-3 beyond 40 cycles) and add them as actual examples with their scope stated.
findings.ruling_reason: This turns on whether the inventor holds data beyond Example 1. [0159] and [0165] record what was not tested: beyond 40 cycles, temperatures other than 22 °C, CO2 cold shock, and PEEK and wiper variants (Examples 2–3 are prophetic, [0154]). The inventor should be asked whether any further results exist. Nothing is to be added without them.

findings.title: Inverted arrangement and purge actuator have no fallback claim
findings.attack: [0117] (ring carried by the poppet, fixed formation deflects it) and [0123] (separate purge actuator, poppet does only its normal stroke) are described as workable and are outside claim 1's 'carried by the core body' and poppet-produced deflection.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add formulations in which the ring is carried by the core body or the poppet and in which a deflecting member movable in response to the pressure differential produces the deflection; supported by [0112], [0117], [0123].
findings.ruling_reason: The separate purge actuator of [0123] is outside claim 1: there 'the poppet (40) perform[s] only its normal stroke', while claim 1 requires that the poppet 'is in over-travel ... and produces a radial deflection'. The inverted arrangement of [0117] is partly answered by the text: [0005] reads 'carried by' as including indirect carriage, so a skirt on a poppet guided by the core body is arguably 'carried by the core body', and the poppet's travel produces the deflection. That argument is contestable, and an explicit fallback supported by [0112], [0117] and [0123] costs nothing. Low stands.

findings.title: No fallback ladder for the austenite finish temperature
findings.attack: If cold or CO2-chilling performance becomes the inventive-step battleground, there is no narrower supported value to retreat to.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If the inventors have target values, add a nested ladder and any specified martensite start temperature; add no values they have not chosen.
findings.ruling_reason: [0073] states that 'No value below 5 °C is specified herein', and [0171] that no martensite start temperature is asserted. A ladder below claims 48 and 74 needs values the inventor has chosen, which is a fact outside the package. The inventor should be asked whether target austenite finish or martensite start values exist. None may be invented.

findings.title: Springless poppet closed by chamber pressure is not disclosed
findings.attack: Every independent product claim recites a return spring; [0122] keeps a single-rate spring even where the ring sets the threshold, so the cheapest design-around (chamber pressure closes the poppet, ring stiffness sets the threshold) has no cover; evidence of conception is weak.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If within the inventors' conception, add that in some embodiments the poppet is biased closed by chamber-side pressure alone and the over-travel threshold is set by the deflectable ring element; otherwise record the boundary.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct on the text: claims 1 and 58 recite a return spring, and [0022] defines it as a 'biasing member'. [0122] keeps a single-rate return spring even where the ring sets the threshold, and chamber pressure is not a member. Whether a springless poppet closed by chamber pressure alone was conceived is for the inventor. If it was not, counsel should record this boundary in the assessment.

findings.title: The diameter measurement convention fails for a wall convoluted along its whole length
findings.attack: With no convolution-free portion, the inner-diameter limitation cannot be measured and a defendant argues it is not met.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a fallback convention to [0028], for example the diameter at the sealing edge (34) or the mean of crest and root diameters.
findings.ruling_reason: [0028] measures the seat ring diameters 'at a portion of the wall free of convolutions'. [0079] allows three or more convolutions, and 'a helical or circumferential wave', between the sealing edge and the retained end, and [0085] requires only that the sealing-edge band be continuous, not free of convolutions. A ring convoluted along its whole length therefore has no measuring location for claims 16 and 67. A fallback convention added now is a clarification. Added after filing, it would be new matter.

findings.title: Pervasive multiple-dependent-claim-on-multiple-dependent-claim defect across 56 claims
findings.attack: Each cited claim multiply depends on a range including an already multiply-dependent claim, contrary to 37 CFR 1.75(c), Rule 43(4) EPC and the aligned UK rule.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Restructure the affected claims' back-reference ranges (split or renumber) so no multiple dependent claim depends on another multiple dependent claim; no narrowing of scope required.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct for the US only. Examples: claim 10 ('any one of claims 1 to 9') takes in claims 8 and 9, each dependent on 'any one of claims 1 to 7', and claim 14 ('11 to 13') takes in claim 13 ('11 or 12'). 37 CFR 1.75(c) bars a multiple dependent claim from serving as the basis for another multiple dependent claim. The finding's statement of EP and UK law is wrong: Rule 43(4) EPC requires only a reference to the claim relied on, and EPO and UKIPO practice accept multiple dependent claims that refer to other multiple dependent claims. Severity corrected from critical to medium. No claim falls: in the US the improper claims are objected to and cured by a preliminary amendment with no loss of scope. The EP and UK sets should keep their dependencies, which give the combination basis relied on in F-36-14. Recommended fix: a US-specific restructured claim set, not a change to the master set.

findings.title: Antecedent basis gap for "bears" in claim 28
findings.attack: "a side on which the poppet bears in over-travel" has no antecedent when claim 28 depends from claim 1 alone, since only claim 2 recites "bears."
findings.least_narrowing_action: Replace "bears" with language tracking claim 1's own vocabulary (contact producing the radial deflection), or restrict claim 28's dependency to claim 2 and its dependents.
findings.ruling_reason: 'Bears' is a verb and needs no antecedent. Claim 28 introduces its own noun with the indefinite article ('a side on which the poppet bears in over-travel'). Claim 1 already has the poppet in over-travel 'produc[ing] a radial deflection of the deflectable ring element', which implies the poppet acts on the ring. [0005] reads 'bears on' as covering direct or indirect contact. Read with claim 1 alone, the side is identifiable.

findings.title: Claim 64 preamble conflicts with the description's definition of "inflatable chamber"
findings.attack: [0025] defines inflatable chamber as the internal volume of the tube, not the tube itself, but claim 64 treats it as the physical article comprising the tube.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Broaden [0025]'s definition to also cover the physical article, or amend claim 64 to the volume-based reading.
findings.ruling_reason: [0025] defines an inflatable chamber as 'the volume ... of a bicycle inner tube or of a tubeless bicycle tyre set-up', and [0001] applies that definition to the claims. Claim 64, however, claims 'An inflatable chamber comprising a bicycle inner tube ... fitted with an inflation valve', which makes a volume comprise a physical article. That is a credible clarity objection. It can be cured without new disclosure by recasting claim 64 as 'A bicycle inner tube or tubeless bicycle tyre set-up fitted with...', with basis in [0139] ('the inflatable chamber so formed ... together with the inflation valve forms a further aspect').

findings.title: Cross-category incorporation of other claims by number within claims 61, 89 and 99
findings.attack: Limitations incorporate entire alternative claim ranges (themselves containing F-37-1 defects) as claim features rather than as formal dependencies, compounding indefiniteness.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Retain the construction once the incorporated ranges are cleaned up under F-37-1; no independent narrowing needed.
findings.ruling_reason: The EPO accepts a claim that refers to a claim of another category ('form a valve core according to any one of claims 1 to 57' in claim 61; claims 89 and 99 likewise). The only live defect is US multiple dependency within the referenced ranges, which is F-37-1. The finding itself proposes no action beyond F-37-1. Duplicate.

findings.title: Dangling final clause in claim 1
findings.attack: The shape-recovery clause is not framed as a fourth named state parallel to the preceding three, creating ambiguity about its status.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Insert a lead-in phrase making the parallel structure explicit.
findings.ruling_reason: Claim 1 ends '...; the deflectable ring element undergoing shape recovery ... when the pressure differential falls below the over-travel threshold' after the list introduced by 'the valve core having:'. The clause is a limitation in any reading and its meaning is plain, so scope is unaffected. Its grammatical status, and whether it belongs to the purge-state limb, is still loose, and 'and wherein the deflectable ring element undergoes shape recovery...' fixes it in place. The same wording is in claim 58. Severity corrected to low: an examiner is unlikely to object, and the fix is cosmetic.

findings.title: Hybrid dependency format in claims 61, 89, 99
findings.attack: Claims 61, 89 and 99 each carry a formal dependency and additionally incorporate a further claim range by reference in the body text ('according to any one of claims X to Y'), leaving ambiguous how the claim should be counted and construed, especially since the incorporated ranges are laden with the F-37-1 defect.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Confirm the intended relationship once F-37-1 is cured; no wording change needed if the intended technique is claim incorporation by reference to a sub-combination.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-37-4, which covers claims 61, 89 and 99. Incorporating a sub-combination by claim reference is an accepted construction, and the only defect in the incorporated ranges is the US one in F-37-1. The finding itself proposes no wording change.

findings.title: Reference numeral (30) conflict between genus claim 1 and species claim 9
findings.attack: Claim 1's genus "deflectable ring element" is numbered (30), the seat ring's own numeral, conflicting with claim 9's equally valid wiper-ring species numbered (132).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete the numeral from claim 1's genus recitation; retain numerals only on the narrowing species claims.
findings.ruling_reason: Claims 1 and 58 give the genus 'deflectable ring element (30)' the seat ring's numeral, while claim 9 makes the wiper ring (132) the deflectable ring element. Rule 43(7) EPC provides that reference signs are not to be construed as limiting, so there is no legal effect, and the premise of a 'conflict' is overstated. Changing to '(30, 132)' or deleting the numeral removes an argument for free. Severity corrected to low.

findings.title: Reference numerals omitted from claims 79-89
findings.attack: Claims 79-89 name the poppet, sealing face, deflectable ring element, main passage, purge gap and purge flow path without any reference numeral, unlike parallel claims 1, 58, 67 and 90-102, creating an internal inconsistency in claim practice.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the existing reference numerals at first mention in claims 79-89, matching claim 1's practice.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct: claims 79–89 carry no numerals, whereas claims 1, 58, 67 and 90–102 do. Rule 43(7) EPC expects reference signs where the application has drawings, and the EPO may ask for them. Numerals should be added only once the drawings exist and are cross-checked (F-36-2). Severity corrected to low: this is formal, with no effect on scope.

findings.title: 'About'/'approximately' used without a stated tolerance
findings.attack: [0007] confirms 'about'/'approximately' carries no defined tolerance unless separately stated, and none is stated for the 0.03 mm interference or the 1.0/3.5 bar values, risking an EPO clarity objection.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a stated tolerance in the description rather than deleting the qualifier from the claims.
findings.ruling_reason: Dependent claims 20, 44 and 101 use 'approximately' or 'about'. [0007] explains the term, and the exact values are separately disclosed ([0156]: '1.0 bar', '3.5 bar'; [0090]: 'in the worked example 1.0 bar ... 3.5 bar'), so the qualifier can be deleted if the EPO objects, with no loss of basis. Adding a stated tolerance now would mean inventing a value the inventor has not given ([0172]: 'The working range of the interference has not been determined'). The proposed fix is barred, and the risk is already covered.

findings.title: 'Chamber side' applied to non-poppet components without antecedent
findings.attack: [0010] defines 'chamber side' only of the poppet; claims 9 and 33 apply 'the chamber side' to the fixed seat and the purge gap respectively without an antecedent covering that usage.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Broaden [0010]'s definition to a general orientation within the valve core rather than a property of the poppet alone (see Prompt 38 Correction); no claim text change needed.
findings.ruling_reason: [0010] defines 'chamber side' only 'of the poppet'. Claim 9 ('the chamber side of the fixed seat') and claim 33 ('the chamber side of the purge gap') use the definite article with no antecedent for that usage, and claim 3 ('the chamber side of the sealing face') has the same pattern. The meaning is clear from [0010] ('open to the inflatable chamber') and [0093], but an antecedent objection is credible. The cure is to restate [0010] as a direction within the valve or to use 'a chamber side' in the claims. Neither needs new disclosure.

findings.title: 112(f) exposure in 'deflecting formation' and 'threshold-setting arrangement'
findings.attack: Both terms combine a generic noun with a function only, risking US means-plus-function construction limited to the disclosed corresponding structures and their equivalents, giving a competitor an escape route via an undisclosed equivalent mechanism.
findings.least_narrowing_action: None required; informational for Prompt 33 litigation assessment. Risk already knowingly accepted per terminology lock.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct, and understated. 'Threshold-setting arrangement' (claim 36) pairs a nonce word with a function and is a likely 35 USC 112(f) term. 'Deflecting formation' (claim 2) is closer to the line. The corresponding structures are disclosed ([0112]–[0116], [0119]–[0122], FIGs. 11 and 14), so the claims are not indefinite. However, [0009] itself says these terms refer to structure 'consistent with the corresponding structures described in this specification and their equivalents', which reads as a 112(f) concession, and it applies the same wording to 'deflectable ring element', the core term of claim 1. Severity corrected to medium: counsel should decide whether to keep that sentence of [0009], because it could narrow claim 1 in the US.

findings.title: Relative term "about" in claim 44
findings.attack: "about" remains a term of degree inviting an EPO Art. 84 clarity objection despite [0007]'s definition.
findings.least_narrowing_action: No pre-emptive action; substitute a stated numeric tolerance if objected to in prosecution.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-37-9 (claim 44, 'about'). It is answered the same way: the exact values of 1.0 bar and 3.5 bar are disclosed in [0090] and [0156], so the qualifier can be deleted in prosecution if objected to. The finding itself proposes no pre-emptive action.

findings.title: Unenumerated single-sentence state definition in claims 1 and 58
findings.attack: The three states are separated only by semicolons in one continuous sentence, increasing the risk of a clarity objection over which limitations belong to which state.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Enumerate the three states (i)/(ii)/(iii); no scope change.
findings.ruling_reason: Claims 1 and 58 introduce each state by its name and its pressure condition ('the closed state, at a pressure differential below a crack pressure, in which...; a normal-open state, at ...; and a purge state, at ...'). Each limitation therefore sits plainly under its named state, and the semicolon-separated list is standard claim form. Numbering (i)–(iii) is optional polish, not a clarity defect.

findings.title: 'Inflatable chamber' defined as a volume but claimed/described as the physical article
findings.attack: [0025] defines 'inflatable chamber' as an immaterial internal volume, but claim 64 claims it as 'comprising a bicycle inner tube' and [0031] equates it directly with the tube — a volume cannot comprise the tube that forms it, exposing claim 64 to a 112(b) indefiniteness attack.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Revise [0025]'s definition to the physical article, matching usage already present throughout the filed text; no new matter.
findings.ruling_reason: [0025] defines the 'inflatable chamber' as 'the volume ... of a bicycle inner tube or of a tubeless bicycle tyre set-up', and [0001] makes that definition govern the claims. Claim 64 ('An inflatable chamber comprising a bicycle inner tube or a tubeless bicycle tyre set-up fitted with an inflation valve'), claim 85 ('the inflatable chamber is a bicycle inner tube') and [0031] ('the inflatable chamber, which is a bicycle inner tube') all use it as the physical article. A volume cannot comprise the tube that bounds it, and a valve stem cannot be 'fixed to' a volume ([0031]). The best defence is that [0010] ('the side open to the inflatable chamber') needs the volume sense, but that sentence works equally well with the article sense ('open to the interior of'). The objection is correct. Severity lowered to medium: the meaning is recoverable and the fix is a one-sentence redefinition in [0025] (the article enclosing a volume) with no loss of scope. It does not threaten claim 64 as a whole.

findings.title: [0078] contradicts the thermally actuated purge embodiment at [0142]
findings.attack: [0078]'s unqualified statement that no heating is involved in reaching the purge state directly contradicts [0142]'s thermally actuated purge, which opens the purge gap by warming.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Qualify [0078] to confine it to the over-travel-actuated embodiments, distinguishing the thermally actuated purge.
findings.ruling_reason: The drafter's defence is strong: [0013] defines the 'purge state' as the state reached above the over-travel threshold, and [0142] calls the thermal variant 'a separate concept ... distinct from the over-travel-actuated purge state' and says it opens the 'purge gap', not the 'purge state'. [0100] draws the same distinction, so read literally, [0078]'s 'no heating ... is involved in reaching the purge state' is true. But [0078] also says 'the load chain is the same in every embodiment: the purge shoulder (44) bears on the deflectable ring element only in over-travel', and that is untrue of [0142], where warming opens the gap without any purge shoulder load. An opponent can quote the two passages against each other. Severity lowered to low: the definitions already resolve the point, and adding 'of the over-travel-actuated embodiments' to [0078] fixes it without touching any claim.

findings.title: Admission that a stainless-steel core body is an obvious corrosion remedy
findings.attack: [0176] characterises the brass-corrosion problem and the stainless-steel solution as 'a matter of general materials knowledge,' handing an examiner/opponent a ready-made obviousness argument against claim 54 standing alone.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reframe [0176] to describe the corrosion consideration without characterising the stainless-steel response as a matter of general knowledge 'for that reason'.
findings.ruling_reason: [0176]: 'Brass is subject to stress-corrosion cracking in ammoniacal environments as a matter of general materials knowledge, and for that reason a core body (20) of stainless steel 303 is described'. This characterises the claim-54 feature (stainless-steel core body) as the known answer to a known problem. At the EPO that is admitted common general knowledge, and in the US it is a binding admission in the specification, so claim 54 loses its fallback value. The best defence is that claim 54 depends on claims 1 to 53 and adds little in any case. That lowers the stake but does not justify an admission that is not needed: [0033] and [0130] already give the corrosion reason without it. Severity lowered to low: the admission affects only one dependent claim, and deleting 'as a matter of general materials knowledge, and for that reason' removes it with no new matter.

findings.title: Admitted sealant-retention drawback in claimed slotted/cellular wall species
findings.attack: [0086] admits the slotted wall, cellular wall and openings-through-the-wall species (claimed in 15 and 32) can themselves retain liquid sealant, undercutting the invention's stated self-cleaning purpose for those specific claimed alternatives.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a sentence noting the air purge acts on these openings too, tempering the admission with the already-disclosed countervailing mechanism.
findings.ruling_reason: Wrong paragraph: the sentence is in [0087] ('Slots, cells and splits that pass through the wall can retain liquid sealant, which is a consideration in choosing between the forms'), not [0086]. And the countervailing mechanism the finding asks for is already in the text. [0086] says these openings 'form the purge opening ... so that inflation gas passes through the wall', [0106] says they are 'opened or uncovered when the purge shoulder (44) strains the wall', and [0111] routes the purge flow path 'through the wall of the deflectable ring element'. A candid statement of a design trade-off does not say that claims 15 or 32 fail to work, and it leaves both claims fully supported. Nothing to amend.

findings.title: Apparent tension between [0078]'s 'no heating' statement and the thermally actuated purge
findings.attack: [0078]'s unqualified statement that 'no heating... is involved in reaching the purge state' appears to contradict [0142]'s later-disclosed thermally actuated purge, which an opponent could cite as an internal contradiction bearing on enablement of, or amendment basis for, the thermal variant.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Scope [0078] explicitly to the mechanically actuated embodiments described in that section.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-38-2: the same [0078]/[0142] tension, the same remedy (confine [0078] to the over-travel-actuated embodiments). It is ruled and routed under F-38-2.

findings.title: Overbroad admission that pre-over-travel operation is conventional
findings.attack: "in the same manner as a conventional valve core" could be read broadly enough to admit the seat ring's sealing role as prior art, beyond the narrower point intended.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Narrow the comparison to the specific crack-pressure/sealing behaviour intended, without touching the purge-gap function.
findings.ruling_reason: The premise is not supported. [0047] says that until the over-travel threshold is reached 'the valve core admits inflation gas and seals in the same manner as a conventional valve core, the seat ring (30) serving only to seat the sealing face (42)'. That describes behaviour, not what the prior art contains. [0029] defines a 'conventional valve core' as one 'lacking a deflectable ring element and a purge gap', so the sentence cannot be read as admitting that a deflectable seat ring, the subject of claims 8 and 30, is known. That a poppet seals on a seat during normal opening is true of every poppet valve and concedes nothing new. [0088] and [0118] use the same comparison consistently.

findings.title: No problem/solution summary precedes the Definitions section (EPO Rule 42(1)(c))
findings.attack: The description opens directly with interpretive Definitions and never states the technical problem and general solution in a single summary paragraph, as EPO Rule 42(1)(c) requires.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a short summary paragraph ahead of the Definitions section stating the problem and solution at a level no narrower than claim 1.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of F-gate14-1, which already covers the missing field, background and summary (the problem-and-solution statement), with the same owner (P4) and remedy. Note on the legal premise: Rule 42(1)(c) EPC requires that the problem and solution can be understood, not a summary paragraph as such. Here they can be pieced together from [0023], [0024] and [0064]-[0065], so the formal risk is lower than the finding states. Handled under F-gate14-1.

findings.title: Inconsistent parenthetical convention for reference numerals in the description
findings.attack: Paragraphs [0031]-[0041] cite numerals without parentheses while [0042] onward use parentheses, contrary to EPC Rule 43(7)'s parenthetical convention.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Standardise [0031]-[0041] to the parenthetical form used from [0042] onward.
findings.ruling_reason: Duplicate of the numeral-style limb of F-gate14-8, which covers the same inconsistency ('seat ring 30' in [0030]-[0041] against 'seat ring (30)' from [0042]) with the same remedy. The legal premise is also wrong: Rule 43(7) EPC governs reference signs in the claims, not the description, so the mismatch in the description is cosmetic. Handled under F-gate14-8.

findings.title: Inconsistent reference-sign practice across the claim set
findings.attack: Claims 79-89 omit reference numerals used consistently for the same components in claims 1, 58, 67 and 90-102.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the existing reference numerals to claims 79-89 at first mention.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct on the text. Independent claims 1, 58, 67 and 90 and claim 100 carry reference signs (e.g. claim 1 'core body (20), a poppet (40)'; claim 90 'seat ring (30) ... sealing edge (34) ... convoluted wall (32)'). Independent method claim 79 and its dependants 80-89 carry none ('a poppet having a supply side, a chamber side and a sealing face, a deflectable ring element ...'). Rule 43(7) EPC expects reference signs where drawings exist and they aid understanding, and an EPO examiner will ask for them in claim 79. Low severity as filed: a formality with no effect on scope, provided the non-limiting statement of F-40a-5 is added.

findings.title: Independent claims not in EPO/UK two-part form
findings.attack: Rule 43(1) EPC requires a two-part preamble/characterising-portion claim form wherever appropriate; the independent claims are single-part throughout.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Defer reformatting to EPO/UK regional-phase entry once the closest prior art is fixed by a search report.
findings.ruling_reason: Claims 1, 58, 67, 79 and 90 are indeed single-part. But Rule 43(1) EPC requires two-part form only 'wherever appropriate', and whether it is appropriate, and where the preamble ends, depends on the closest prior art. That is fixed by the search report, not by the saved set: prior-art/INDEX.md records 'Coverage is thin. A professional search is warranted'. Recasting now against a guessed closest reference would risk putting features into the preamble that are then conceded as known. Resolved by the EPO/UKIPO search report; counsel decides at regional-phase entry. Change nothing in the fix pass.

findings.title: No statement that reference signs in the claims are non-limiting
findings.attack: Absence of the customary disclaimer sharpens the risk of numerals in the claims being read as limiting (see F-37-3).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a standard non-limiting reference-sign disclaimer sentence at [0001].
findings.ruling_reason: [0001] says only that the numerals 'are those of the drawings' and that an illustrated embodiment 'does not limit' a defined term. It says nothing about reference signs in the claims. The risk is concrete: claim 1 attaches the seat-ring numeral to the genus ('a deflectable ring element (30)'), and claim 2 attaches the purge-shoulder numeral to the genus ('a deflecting formation (44)'). A competitor could argue those genera are confined to the numbered species. Rule 43(7) EPC already makes reference signs non-limiting at the EPO, but there is no equivalent statutory rule in US claim construction, so the sentence adds real protection at no cost. Low: this is a one-sentence addition to [0001].

findings.title: Abstract, drawing sheets, brief description of drawings and field/background/summary absent; [0160] refers to a missing background
findings.attack: An abstract is required in the US, at the EPO and in the UK; a brief description of the drawings is required by 37 CFR 1.74 and EPC Rule 42(1)(d). Drawings relied on throughout but not filed trigger EPO Rule 56 and US 35 U.S.C. 113 consequences. [0160]'s cross-reference points to no background section.
findings.least_narrowing_action: The owning drafter supplies the abstract, the list of figures, the field/background/summary and the drawing sheets (from stripped instructions), and points [0160] at the background or rewords it to 'both failure modes, leak-down and blockage, as defined herein'.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct on the package. It contains a description beginning at '#### Definitions and conventions' [0001], the claims, and figures.md, which is a figure plan ('Their content is known only from the README's one-line descriptions'), not drawing sheets. There is no abstract, no brief description of the drawings, and no field, background or summary. [0160] says the conventional cores 'exhibited both of the failure modes described in the background', but no background exists. The description relies on FIGS. 1-15 throughout (e.g. [0030], [0053], [0081], [0113]). Filed without drawings, this triggers Rule 56 EPC (the date moves or the references are deleted) and 35 U.S.C. 113. If the abstract and list of figures are produced at a later step outside this package, that limb closes there; the missing drawings, the missing summary and the [0160] cross-reference remain. High is right: filed as is, the date or the figure-based support is at risk. The drawings need the inventor's sketches (a disclosure request).

findings.title: Axial layout of seat ring, sealing edge, internal shoulder and chamber-side purge shoulder cannot be reconstructed from the text
findings.attack: The poppet opens towards the chamber, so the sealing face lies on the chamber side of the sealing edge; a purge shoulder on the chamber side of the sealing face then moves away from a ring whose 2.3 mm bore admits only the stem, and [0116] puts the sealing edge at the supply-side end. With no drawing sheets, the preferred embodiment of claims 3 and 4 cannot be built from the words (Art. 83/84; 112(a)).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add one paragraph, from the inventor's FIG-1 sketch, stating the axial order of the parts, and draw it; if the shoulder is not on the chamber side of the sealing face, conform [0021], [0038], [0112] and claim 3.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct on the text. [0046]: to open, the poppet 'moves ... towards the chamber side, lifting the sealing face (42) from the sealing edge (34)', so the sealing face sits on the chamber side of the sealing edge. [0021], [0038] and [0112] then place the purge shoulder 'on the chamber side of the sealing face', so it moves further from the sealing edge as the poppet opens. [0088] makes the ring bore (2.3 mm, [0089]) admit only 'the poppet stem (41)'. [0116] puts the chamber-side end of the seat ring 'remote from the sealing edge', implying the ring extends chamber-ward from the edge. No paragraph explains how a ring whose bore takes only the stem can present a surface on the chamber side of the poppet head for the shoulder to reach in over-travel. [0038] only asserts the result ('contacts the seat ring 30 only during over-travel'). Best defence: claim 1 is functional and [0105], [0113] and [0116] describe other workable arrangements, so claim 1 itself is not left without an enabled form. But claims 3 and 4 and the tested embodiment cannot be rebuilt from the words, and there are no drawings (F-gate14-1). High stands. It is resolved only by the inventor's FIG-1 sketch or an account of the axial order of the parts, which is a disclosure request.

findings.title: Claim structure not adapted to US multiple-dependency rules or EPO Rule 43(2)
findings.attack: Multiple dependent claims serve as the basis for other multiple dependent claims (for example claim 10 on claims 8 and 9, claim 13 via claim 10, claims 61, 64, 89 and 99), which is improper under 35 U.S.C. 112(e) and 37 CFR 1.75(c): such claims are not examined on the merits. There are three or more independent product claims (1, 58, 67), which needs a Rule 43(2) justification; the 102 claims also carry excess-claim fees in all three offices.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Counsel prepares a US claim set with single dependencies and prepares the EPO interrelated-products justification; no scope is narrowed.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct on the claims. Claim 10 ('any one of claims 1 to 9') rests on the multiple dependent claims 8 and 9 ('any one of claims 1 to 7'). Claim 13 ('claim 11 or claim 12') rests indirectly on claim 10. Claims 61 and 89 refer to 'any one of claims 1 to 57' and claim 99 to 'any one of claims 67 to 78', which themselves contain multiple dependents. 37 CFR 1.75(c) and MPEP 608.01(n) bar a multiple dependent claim from serving as the basis of another, directly or indirectly. Claims 1, 58 and 67 are three independent product claims, which need a Rule 43(2)(a) EPC interrelated-products justification (plausible here: component, valve core and valve). The claim count of 102 carries substantial excess-claim fees at the EPO, the USPTO and the UKIPO. Severity lowered to medium: every point is cured by reformatting and a justification without narrowing, and none is a patentability rejection. It is a counsel decision at national/regional entry (US claim set, fee strategy).

findings.title: Illustrated embodiment's outward deflection said to open an outer-surface clearance that the description says needs inward movement
findings.attack: Outward movement of the outer surface towards the core body bore narrows the clearance between them and cannot open it; [0103] itself says such a gap opens by inward movement. The only built embodiment and FIG. 3/10B as instructed therefore depict a mechanism the specification rules out. The FIG. 1 instructions draw a clearance at rest, contradicting 'purge gap closed'. This draws Art. 84/112 objections against claims 29 and 30 and undermines the evidential weight of Example 1.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Get the inventor to confirm the prototype's actual kinematics, then conform [0020], [0040], [0053], [0054], [0093] and the FIG. 1/3/6/10B instructions (using the wording of [0103] if the gap opens by inward movement). No claim narrowing.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct on the text. [0040] and [0053] place the purge gap of the illustrated embodiment between 'the outer surface of the seat ring (30) and the core body bore (22)'. [0020] and [0054] say the illustrated deflection 'is outward', and [0093] does the same for the wiper ring ('deflects the wiper ring (132) radially outward, opening the purge gap ... between the outer surface of the wiper ring (132) and the core body bore (22)'). But [0103] says such a gap 'opens where the bounding portion of the outer surface ... moves away from the core body bore (22). That movement may be an inward movement', which is the only kinematics consistent with the geometry: outward movement closes that clearance. Separately, [0036], [0053] and [0103] say the non-interference remainder of the outer surface is 'free of the core body bore', which reads as a clearance at rest, against [0040] 'In the closed state the purge gap 60 is closed'. Best defence: claim 29 (outward) is supported by the third arrangement [0105], and claim 30 by the inward movement of [0103], so each claim alone has a coherent basis. But the only built embodiment, Example 1 ([0155]-[0159]) and the FIG. 3/10B instructions describe a mechanism the specification itself rules out, which undermines the example's evidential weight and invites Art. 83/84 and 112(a)/(b) objections. High stands. The prototype's actual kinematics are an inventor fact, so this goes out as a disclosure request.

findings.title: Wipe-only embodiment disclosed but outside every independent claim
findings.attack: A competitor seals the ring periphery so that no purge flow path exists and keeps the over-travel deflection and recovery wipe of the sealing face. [0167] shows the clean surfaces are the wiped ones. This escapes claims 1, 58 and 79 (all require the purge gap and purge flow path), and escapes claim 67 outside the dimensional window.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent valve-core claim, supported by [0065], [0124] and [0061], reciting over-travel radial deflection of the ring and recovery movement across a poppet surface, without the purge gap; claim 1 is kept.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct. [0065] expressly discloses an embodiment in which the cleaning action is 'provided by the snap-back wipe alone, the deflectable ring element being sealed at its periphery so that no inflation gas flows past it'. [0167] records that the clean surfaces after testing were the wiped ones (sealing edge and sealing face). Claims 1, 58 and 79 each require the purge gap to open and a purge flow path 'from the supply side through the purge gap', so a peripherally sealed wipe-only core escapes all three. Claim 67 is bounded by an inner diameter of 2.0-2.6 mm and a wall of 0.15-0.30 mm, so a seat ring outside that window escapes it too. In the US, subject matter disclosed but not claimed is at risk of being dedicated to the public. Support for the proposed independent claim is in [0061], [0065] and [0124]. On the saved art, no reference discloses recovery of the seat itself wiping the poppet (INDEX coverage statement; #3, #7 and #12 use separate wipers or rotation). High stands. Whether to add the claim, and how it fits unity, is a counsel decision.

findings.title: 'About', 'approximately' and 'nominally' in claims while [0007] disclaims any tolerance
findings.attack: [0007] states the qualifiers define no numerical tolerance, removing the guidance needed to construe them; this draws an Art. 84/112(b) objection, and in litigation these fallbacks become point values or indefinite.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite the disclosed worked values without the qualifier in these fallback claims, or add a tolerance only if the inventor has one.
findings.ruling_reason: The premise that [0007] 'remov[es] the guidance needed to construe them' is false. [0007] gives the standard: the qualifier 'accounts for ordinary variation arising from manufacturing tolerance and measurement, consistent with the level of precision of the surrounding disclosure'. It gives worked instances for both 'approximately 0.03 mm' (claims 20, 101) and 'nominally 55.8 wt%' (claims 49, 75, 98). Declining to assert a measured tolerance band is honest, because none was measured ([0172]). It does not make the terms indefinite. US law accepts 'about' where the intrinsic record supplies a standard of precision, and the EPO objects to 'about' mainly where the value is relied on to distinguish over prior art, which is not yet the case for any of these fallbacks. Note for counsel: if one of these values is later relied on to distinguish, drop the qualifier at that point.

findings.title: [0009] invites means-plus-function construction of deflectable ring element, deflecting formation and threshold-setting arrangement
findings.attack: The wording 'any structure capable of performing the recited function, consistent with the corresponding structures described ... and their equivalents' concedes a 35 U.S.C. 112(f)-style construction, limiting the central claim-1 term to the described structures and their equivalents in US litigation.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Replace the second sentence of [0009] with structural definitions (as in [0014], [0021], [0022]) and delete 'corresponding structures ... and their equivalents'; counsel to consider structural wording in claim 36.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct for the US. The second sentence of [0009] says each functional term 'refers to any structure capable of performing the recited function, consistent with the corresponding structures described in this specification and their equivalents; this specification describes at least one corresponding structure for each such term'. That copies the language of 35 U.S.C. 112(f) ('corresponding structure ... described in the specification and equivalents thereof') and invites the court to treat 'deflecting formation', 'threshold-setting arrangement' (a nonce-type word) and 'deflectable ring element' in claims 1, 2 and 36 as means-plus-function terms, confined to the described species and their equivalents. Best defence: [0014], [0021] and [0022] give structural definitions ('any annular element, carried by the valve core'), and many species are described, so 112(f) scope would still be fairly wide. But [0009] works against those definitions, and the intended construction is broader than 112(f) allows. No EPO or UK equivalent. Medium stands (US scope).

findings.title: Figure plan and registry carry internal working references, stale flags and a FIG. 6A call-out mismatch
findings.attack: The instructions contain dossier references (11.md, 13.md, 14.md, DA codes, Prompt 20 Assumption A2), prejudicial statements ('cannot be closed without new matter', 'the inventor states doubt'), and a deferred cross-check that is now stale. [0089] says the dimensions are called out in FIG. 6A, but the instructions call out none. Numeral style is inconsistent ('seat ring 30' in [0030]-[0041] against 'seat ring (30)' from [0042]).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Strip all internal references from the instructions before the drawings are commissioned, add the dimension call-outs to FIG. 6A, re-run the registry cross-check, and unify the numeral style to parentheses.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct on figures.md. It carries dossier references ('`14.md`', '`11.md`, `12.md`', 'DA-7, DA-23, DA-24', '01 Q22', 'Prompt 16 (blueprint) has not yet run'), which are now stale because the description exists. It also carries prejudicial statements ('entries that cannot be closed without new matter', 'the inventor states doubt about pursuing it'). These must not reach a draughtsman or the file, where they could be discovered. [0089] says the seat ring inner diameter, wall thickness, free length and convolution amplitude 'are called out in FIG. 6A', but the FIG. 6 entry calls out only 'the purge gap and its opening dimension' (6B). Numeral style is inconsistent: 'seat ring 30' in [0030]-[0041], 'seat ring (30)' from [0042] (this absorbs F-40a-2). registry.md is not in the review package, so the registry cross-check limb is not verified here. Medium stands.

findings.title: Kit has no claim and the component claim is dimension-bound
findings.attack: A supplier sells the matched seat ring, poppet and spring kit without a core body, or a seat ring outside claim 67's Presta window; only uncertain indirect infringement is then available.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a kit claim supported by [0141] (matched seat ring, poppet with purge shoulder and two-stage return spring giving the claim-1 states when assembled into a core body).
findings.ruling_reason: Correct. [0141] discloses a kit of seat ring, poppet with sealing face and purge shoulder, and two-stage return spring, 'matched so that, when assembled into the core body (20), the purge shoulder (44) is spaced from the seat ring (30) throughout the normal stroke and bears on the seat ring (30) only in over-travel'. [0180] and FIG. 5 repeat it. No claim covers the kit: claim 1 requires the core body, and claim 67 is limited to an inner diameter of 2.0-2.6 mm and a wall of 0.15-0.30 mm. The finding overstates slightly: contributory infringement (US 35 U.S.C. 271(c); UK s.60(2)) is realistically available against a matched kit. But a direct kit claim removes the knowledge and intent elements and the need to prove a direct infringer. Support is in [0141]. Medium stands.

findings.title: Over-travel by depressor, by hand, during deflation only, or by a separate purge actuator falls outside claims 1, 58 and 79
findings.attack: Claim 1 defines the purge state by 'a pressure differential exceeding the over-travel threshold' with the poppet itself in over-travel. A depressor-only core (Schrader, or Presta with an adaptor), a deflation-only core, or the purge-actuator design ('the poppet performing only its normal stroke') arguably has no such state.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate the claim-1 purge state as over-travel produced by the pressure differential exceeding the threshold or by mechanical depression of the poppet (support [0066]), and add a claim to the purge-actuator form (support [0123]).
findings.ruling_reason: Correct in substance. Claim 1 defines the purge state as 'at a pressure differential exceeding the over-travel threshold, in which the poppet is in over-travel', and claim 79 requires 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold'. Claim 46 adds depressor actuation only 'additionally', so it does not help. [0066] discloses over-travel 'produced, in addition or instead, by mechanical depression ... whatever the pressure differential', with the second spring stage omitted. [0067] discloses purge 'during deflation only, each inflation event using the normal stroke alone'. [0123] discloses a separate purge actuator with 'the poppet (40) performing only its normal stroke'. The purge-actuator form plainly falls outside claims 1, 58 and 79. The depressor-only and deflation-only forms can argue that no pressure-driven purge state exists; the drafter's best reply, that some pressure differential would always overcome the spring, is weak where an over-travel stop or a very stiff stage prevents it. All three are disclosed but unclaimed, which is a US dedication risk. Support for the reformulation is in [0066], [0067] and [0123]. Medium stands: these forms mostly suit the Schrader and deflation markets ([0123], [0137]).

findings.title: No ranges for normal stroke, interference or shape-setting window
findings.attack: The normal stroke and axial clearance, the interference and the shape-setting time/temperature are given as single values only, leaving single-point fallbacks for parameters a teardown can measure.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Ask the inventor for ranges they actually conceived; do not generate them.
findings.ruling_reason: Correct on the text. The normal stroke is given only as '0.6 mm' ([0046], [0090]), with no range. For the interference, [0172] says 'The working range of the interference has not been determined' (claims 20 and 101 recite approximately 0.03 mm). For shape-setting, [0148] gives only '500 °C for 10 minutes' and [0175] confirms 'the values used for the prototype ... and not a process window' (claim 94). The fallbacks for these parameters are therefore single points that a teardown can measure and a competitor can step around. The ranges must come from the inventor and must not be generated. Low stands. Disclosure request.
